target.title: fix(gateway): reap stale MCP processes on session reset regardless of…
target.body:
Closes #92569

## What Problem This Solves

Resetting or deleting a session could leave its MCP child processes alive when the active agent run exceeded the 15-second cleanup grace period. Those stale children could retain SQLite/LadybugDB write locks or ports until idle-TTL cleanup.

## Why This Is the Best Fix

Gateway lifecycle cleanup now requests required, lease-aware MCP retirement before aborting or waiting. The MCP manager owns the distinction between ordinary deferred retirement, which later reuse may cancel, and reset/delete retirement, which survives late runtime creation or reuse. Embedded and reply-backed run waiters follow replacements until the session becomes idle. Materialized run/view/request lease release completes deferred disposal.

The implementation also closes two overlap windows: a replacement registering after a waiter settles, and a new reset beginning while an earlier runtime disposal is still pending. Immediate gateway disposal was rejected because it can close transports under in-flight MCP work; TTL-only cleanup is nondeterministic. Heavy embedded-agent and MCP cleanup modules now load only when reset/delete cleanup runs, so read-only status startup does not pay for those lifecycle dependencies.

## User Impact

Session reset/delete no longer strands old MCP processes on the timeout path. Active MCP work remains alive until its final lease releases, then the old runtime and child process retire deterministically.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `28fa82fbc67bd930bcc2735b95f40e72286aac12`
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29568843591
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`
- Result: 6 files, 299 tests passed across gateway, auto-reply, agent, and E2E shards.
- Formatting/lint: all 20 changed TypeScript files pass `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --deny-warnings`; `git diff --check` passes.
- Real stdio proof: an MCP child remains alive while a lease is held, then exits after final release: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29503144525
- Real lock proof: the regression child holds an SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` write lock during deferred retirement; final lease release terminates the child and lets the parent acquire the lock.

Regression coverage includes reset/delete success and timeout, retries, embedded and reply-backed runs, same-session replacements, waiter-settlement races, overlapping disposal, late runtime creation/reuse, active lease preservation, real child exit, and real SQLite lock release.

## Risk and Compatibility

- No config, storage schema, protocol, dependency, UI, or plugin API changes.
- Active consumers remain protected by aggregate leases across static and requester-scoped runtimes.
- Cleanup failures remain best-effort and logged, matching the existing lifecycle contract.

target.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite
target.body:
Closes #109842

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where native MCP OAuth credentials and authorization state used a separate JSON-plus-file-lock store. That storage model sat outside OpenClaw's canonical state database and made refresh, logout, migration, and cross-process conflict handling depend on filesystem behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

MCP OAuth now uses the shared SQLite state database as its only runtime store. Login, refresh, logout, resource challenges, and terminal token rejection run under a shared SQLite lease; the HTTP transport keeps authorization retries inside that fenced owner. `openclaw doctor --fix` is the sole legacy migration owner: it imports exact validated JSON under exclusive state ownership, records a receipt, verifies cleanup, and never creates a runtime fallback.

The migration intentionally does not dual-read or dual-write. Malformed, ambiguous, changing, or contended legacy state remains in place with actionable Doctor output. A replacement token rejected by the resource is marked for explicit reauthorization, preventing refresh loops across later requests.

AI-assisted implementation. I reviewed the storage, migration, OAuth, MCP SDK, and Codex projection paths and understand the resulting ownership model.

## User Impact

New MCP OAuth sessions persist only in `state/openclaw.sqlite`. Existing installations with files under `state/mcp-oauth` must run `openclaw doctor --fix`; valid credentials are imported and the retired JSON is removed only after verification. Corrupt or actively owned files fail closed.

Operators gain serialized cross-process refresh and logout behavior, request cancellation during OAuth work, preserved challenge metadata, and a clear explicit-login path when refreshed credentials are rejected.

Release note: MCP OAuth credentials and refresh state now persist in SQLite. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` once to import legacy MCP OAuth JSON.

## Evidence

- 86 focused state-lease, OAuth resolver, bearer retry, transport, and Doctor migration tests pass across four Vitest shards.
- Blacksmith Testbox changed gate passed formatting, generated baselines, core and test typechecks, full core lint, Kysely/database-first guards, SDK boundaries, import cycles, and architecture checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29567071520

- Source-blind CLI smoke emitted only the normal shared SQLite bootstrap state and no retired OAuth JSON, JSONL, TXT, or lock sidecar.

target.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling a browser tab operation during the reachability retry delay would wait the full delay before responding to the cancellation.

`ensureBrowserRunning` used `new Promise(setTimeout)` for the 250ms retry delay between reachability probes. When the request `AbortSignal` fired during this delay, the function waited the entire `TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS` before calling `signal.throwIfAborted()`, adding unnecessary latency to cancellation-sensitive callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry delay now uses `sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal)` which rejects immediately when the signal fires, so the caller is notified of the cancellation during the delay rather than after it.

The `sleepWithAbort` rejection is caught (`.catch(() => {}))` and the original abort reason is rethrown via `signal?.throwIfAborted()`. This preserves the caller's original error message in the response body rather than surfacing the generic `"aborted"` from `sleepWithAbort`.

Related prior art: #108561 (discord gateway READY retry abortSignal), #108408 (feishu retry abortSignal propagation).

## User Impact

Browser tab operations (close, focus, select) cancelled during the 250ms reachability retry window respond to user cancellation up to 200ms faster — dropping from ~250ms to ~50ms.

## Evidence

### Scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `551d358f243` |
| Files | `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts` (+7/−4) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/proof-abort-timing.test.ts` (+166) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/proof-real-browser-timing.test.ts` (+215) |
| Net | +388 / −4 across 3 files |

### Production change (behavior)

```ts
// Before
await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_DELAY_MS); });
signal?.throwIfAborted();

// After
await sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal).catch(() => {});
signal?.throwIfAborted();
```

### Production-route real-timer timing proof

Exercises the actual `registerBrowserTabRoutes` route handler with **real** `performance.now()` timers — not fake timers or copied helper logic. The handler processes a `/tabs/action (close)` request against a mock profile where `isReachable` returns `false`, triggering the retry delay. An abort fires 50ms into the 250ms retry window.

**BEFORE** (old code — `new Promise(setTimeout)`):

```
  === PR #109536 — Production-Route Real-Timer Proof ===
  Status:           500
  Response body:    {"error":"Error: cancelled"}
  Reachability probes: 1
  Total elapsed:    252.4ms
  Threshold:        < 150ms ✗ FAIL (expected with old code)
  ================================================
```

The old code **waits the full 250ms retry delay** before noticing the abort. The caller sees the `"Error: cancelled"` abort reason (from `throwIfAborted`), but only after the timer completes.

**AFTER** (new code — `sleepWithAbort`):

```
  === PR #109536 — Production-Route Real-Timer Proof ===
  Status:           500
  Response body:    {"error":"Error: cancelled"}
  Reachability probes: 1
  Total elapsed:    53.2ms
  Threshold:        < 150ms ✓
  ================================================
```

The new code **cancels in ~53ms** — as soon as the abort signal fires during the retry delay. The original `"Error: cancelled"` abort reason is preserved (no generic `"aborted"` leak).

Same error body, same behavior invariant — but ~200ms faster response to cancellation.

### Real-browser timing proof (Chrome 138)

Launches a real headless Chrome instance, probes its CDP endpoint to confirm reachability, then measures the old vs new retry timing using the actual production-route `sleepWithAbort` import from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`. Chrome is verified reachable before the timing test.

**Environment:**
```
Chrome version: Chrome/138.0.7204.157 (headless)
CDP endpoint:   http://127.0.0.1:19438/json/version
```

**OLD code (setTimeout — abort fires at 50ms, ignored for full delay):**
```
  Trial 1: 251.1ms
  Trial 2: 250.3ms
  Trial 3: 250.8ms
  → Average: 250.7ms  — waits full 250ms delay
```

**NEW code (sleepWithAbort — abort cancels immediately):**
```
  Trial 1: 50.7ms
  Trial 2: 50.6ms
  Trial 3: 51.3ms
  → Average: 50.9ms  — aborts in ~50ms
```

**Abort reason preservation:** ✓ `"tab operation cancelled by user"` propagated correctly

**Summary:**
```
Old code (setTimeout):      ~251ms  waits full 250ms delay
New code (sleepWithAbort):  ~51ms   aborts in ~50ms
Improvement:                ~200ms faster
Environment:                Chrome Chrome/138.0.7204.157 on Linux
```

### Regression coverage

The existing fake-timer test `"does not retry or mutate after cancellation during the retry delay"` (`tabs.test.ts:324`) continues to pass. The new real-timer proof test `"aborts promptly during the retry delay (real timers)"` adds production-route coverage with actual wall-clock timing guarantees. The new real-browser proof test `"demonstrates old vs new retry timing with a real Chrome instance"` adds real-browser coverage with Chrome 138 headless.

### Local gates (touched surface)

| Gate | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/` | **24 passed** / 3 files |

---

target.title: perf(ci): O(1) boundary sticky key and 32 vCPU for the ext-package-boundary lane
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

check-additional-extension-package-boundary became the light-run critical-path pole (3.5–4min) after the 32vcpu bump cut check-lint/deps/build to ~2min. Measured breakdown (runs 29564442266/29564411446/29564259862, 8vcpu): ~40s cold Node setup + 142–161s shard step — ~101s cold plugin-sdk dts prep (9 parallel tsgo builds) + ~58s compiling 122 plugins at concurrency 6 — because both sticky disks 429 at Blacksmith's 1000-disk installation cap and the boundary sticky was itself per-PR × per-config-hash keyed, a direct contributor to that saturation. A warm main-push reference ran the same shard in 67s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **O(1) re-key of the ext-boundary sticky** (the #109752 pattern): key drops to `<repo>-ext-boundary-v2`; the config/scripts/lockfile hash moves from the key into the in-job `.source-trees` marker (identical fingerprint composition in all three gates), alongside the existing tree-OID + node/pnpm fingerprint. Single semantic writer: the boundary lane commits with explicit `commit: true` on non-PR events (not if-missing — first-seed heuristics can strand stale markers); PR mounts and the check-lint consumer stay `commit: "false"`. The seed step is writer-only (drops an 11s PR-side re-seed) and clears `.snapshot-ready`/`.source-trees` first so a partial seed cannot publish as valid. The snapshot refreshes on every main push, keeping PR tree-OID matches warm.
- **Runner 8→32 vCPU + `OPENCLAW_EXTENSION_BOUNDARY_CONCURRENCY` 6→16**: the 9-way dts prep and the 122 tsgo compiles both scale with cores at similar billed core-minutes (same precedent as check-lint/deps/build).
- Node-deps setup needed no change — the lane already consumes the #109752 v3 snapshot key once mount capacity returns.
- New guards pin the O(1) key, single-writer commit expression, read-only consumers, fingerprint parity across gates, writer-only seed, the 32vcpu row, and concurrency 16.

## User Impact

None at runtime — CI-only. Expected pole after the operator-side stale-disk purge: warm PR runs ~1.5min or less; cold (boundary-touching) runs ~2min via the core bump.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 77 passed; `pnpm check:test-types` green; `actionlint` clean; sibling pin tests green (plugin-prerelease; package-acceptance runner-pin assertions passed — its 3 stderr-empty failures are local shell-rc noise unrelated to this diff).

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
@
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Rebase Note

Rebased onto current main (9ddd988c9) to pick up the rename `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout`. The private helper `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` is now re-exported for direct testing.

## What Changed (vs previous revision)

- **Rebased onto main**: Resolved merge conflicts with the `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` rename and added test for stalled DNS preflight.
- **Re-exported `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo`**: The function was un-exported during the main rename; re-exported so bounded-read tests can target it directly.
- **Fixed lint**: Added curly braces to `if (res.destroyed) return;` one-liners in the test (eslint `curly`).

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

target.title: fix(android): keep composer media with its chat

[AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves Android composer state was not consistently bound to the active Gateway, agent, and session. Drafts, picked or shared media, voice notes, delayed send results, optimistic messages, cached history, and durable outbox rows could therefore be displayed or retried under a replacement chat owner. ## Why This Change Was Made The composer now uses one explicit owner identity across UI state, async callbacks, send admission, pending-run projection, cache reads, session metadata, and outbox recovery. The last verified default agent is retained only for the same Gateway during reconnects and is persisted for offline process restart. Owner-mismatched unscoped outbox rows remain visible for manual recovery, but cannot be retried against the current owner. Session deletion events now always carry the resolved agent owner. ## User Impact Drafts and media stay with the chat where they started. Switching Gateway, agent, or session no longer lets stale picker, share, voice-note, send, history, or outbox work mutate the replacement chat. Offline reconnects continue using the last verified owner for the same Gateway, while ambiguous recovery rows require explicit re-entry or deletion instead of unsafe replay. ## Evidence ### Contributor behavior proof The original issue was reproduced and verified on an Android API 36 emulator paired to an isolated Gateway: creating a replacement chat previously retained an unsent attachment; the patched app cleared it. The maintainer expansion preserves that behavior and applies the same owner contract to adjacent state surfaces.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves `parseFeishuMessageContent` used an empty `catch {}` that silently swallowed `JSON.parse` failures. The prior fix added `formatErrorMessage(err)` to the log, but V8 `JSON.parse` error messages can include the malformed input content — risking message content leakage in verbose logs. ## Why This Change Was Made **Security:** `formatErrorMessage(err)` performs pattern-based redaction only, and does not guarantee removal of arbitrary user message content from V8 error messages. A malformed Feishu message body could leak to operator logs. The fix replaces the exception-derived log text with safe metadata (message type, message ID) while preserving the raw-content fallback. ## User Impact - **Before (empty catch):** Bad JSON parse errors were invisible to operators. - **Before (formatErrorMessage):** Error text could leak message content through V8 JSON.parse error messages. - **After:** Verbose/debug logging records only safe metadata — `feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_xxx)` — never the exception message or raw content. Callers still receive the raw content string as fallback. ## Code Changes ### `send.ts` | Change | Detail | |--------|--------| | `parseFeishuMessageContent` | Added `messageId?: string` parameter for richer diagnostics | | `catch` block | Removed `formatErrorMessage(err)` — logs only `msgType` + `messageId` | | `parseFeishuMessageItem` | Passes `item.message_id` through to the parse function | | Imports | Removed `formatErrorMessage` from `error-runtime` | **Before (unsafe):** ```typescript catch (err) { logVerbose(`feishu message content parse failed: ${formatErrorMessage(err)}`); return rawContent; } ``` **After (safe):** ```typescript catch { const safeId = messageId ? ` (id: ${messageId})` : ""; logVerbose(`feishu message content parse failed for ${msgType} message${safeId}`); return rawContent; } ``` ### `send.test.ts` - New test: `logs a safe diagnostic (not raw content) when message content is not valid JSON` - Asserts `mockLogVerbose` is called with safe metadata - Asserts `mockLogVerbose` is NOT called with raw content `{bad json}` - Asserts the return value preserves the raw content as fallback ## Evidence **Head SHA:** `085013da12d` **Base:** `77f9da5461d` ### 1. target.title: improve(ci): replace boundary guards with focused Oxlint rules
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two checks in `check-additional-boundaries-a` launch custom TypeScript AST scripts for syntax-only rules: deprecated `registerHttpHandler(...)` calls and raw UI `window.open(...)` calls. The raw-window script also still scanned the retired `ui/src/ui` tree, so it no longer guarded the live Control UI owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces both scripts with focused Oxlint JS rules behind `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`. Focused mode retains wrapper-owned process and sparse-checkout handling while skipping unrelated type-aware policy, artifact preparation, and the shared heavy-check lock.

Exact legacy semantics are retained:

| Rule | Roots | Reports | Intentionally ignores |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registerHttpHandler` | `src`, `extensions`; `.ts` production files | Static-property call expressions on any receiver, including parenthesized/type-asserted/non-null/optional-chain forms | Computed access, property references, destructuring, comments/strings, test/harness suffixes |
| raw `open` | live owner `ui/src`; `.ts` production files | Static `window.open` or `globalThis.open` calls, including parenthesized/type-asserted/non-null/optional-chain forms | Computed/nested receivers, property references, destructuring, `satisfies`, comments/strings, test/harness suffixes, the two owning helper modules |

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two catalog rollback guards compared timestamps returned by `Date.parse` without checking for `NaN`:

1. `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts`
2. `isMonotonicRollback` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-snapshot-store.ts`

Both used `Date.parse(candidate.generatedAt) < Date.parse(current.generatedAt)`. When either `generatedAt` string is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `Date.parse` returns `NaN`, and `NaN < NaN` evaluates to `false`. The rollback guards therefore reported "not a rollback" and accepted a candidate that should have been rejected, allowing the catalog snapshot store to move backward to an older or malformed snapshot.

## Fix

Mirror the same defensive policy in both guards:
- If the **candidate's** `generatedAt` is invalid (`NaN`), conservatively treat it as a rollback so malformed candidates cannot downgrade the store.
- If the **current** snapshot's `generatedAt` is invalid, treat the candidate as newer (not a rollback) so a broken current state can still be repaired.

Export `isHostedCatalogSignedFeedRollback` and `isMonotonicRollback` as named exports (instead of wrapping in `__testing`) so the knip production deadcode scan does not flag them as unused. Both functions are already called from production code.

## Evidence

- **Local test run** (10 regression tests pass):
  ```
  RUN  v4.1.9
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed | 35 skipped (45)
  ```
- **New tests cover**: candidate invalid → rollback; current invalid → not a rollback; equal-sequence timestamp comparison; newer/older by sequence.
- **No production behavior change**: the sequence-based fast path is unchanged; the timestamp branch only changes for invalid timestamps.

target.title: fix(infra): gateway pid probe no longer hangs when ps sampling stalls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readGatewayProcessArgsSync` (in `src/infra/gateway-processes.ts`) probes `ps` on darwin to read a gateway process's argv **before** signaling it or reporting it as a verified listener PID. The darwin branch already passed a 1000ms timeout, but {BT}spawnSync{BT} defaults `killSignal` to SIGTERM, which an unresponsive or hung `ps` child can ignore. As a result a stalled `ps` probe can keep the gateway process blocked past the configured timeout, hanging gateway signal verification and listener PID discovery.

This is the same class of stall already fixed for the doctor TUI process probe in #109243, applied to the gateway's own pid-verification path.

## Evidence

- The fix adds `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `spawnSync("ps", ...)` call so a stalled probe is reaped at the deadline instead of hanging, and extracts the timeout into a named `GATEWAY_PS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` constant.
- Local vitest run of `src/infra/gateway-processes.test.ts` is green: 8 passed (8), including the darwin path.
- The darwin test now asserts the full `spawnSync` options shape - encoding, killSignal, timeout - locking in the behavior (mirrors the assertion added in #109243).

```ts
const ps = spawnSync("ps", ["-o", "command=", "-p", String(pid)], {
  encoding: "utf8",
  killSignal: "SIGKILL",
  timeout: GATEWAY_PS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS,
});
```

target.title: improve: let Code Mode use declared tool result shapes
target.body:
Related: #109288
Follow-up to #109651 and #109290

AI-assisted: Yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode learned exact tool ids and compact input signatures from #109651, but every tool result still appeared as unknown. Even when a tool had a stable structured result, models often spent one exec returning the raw value and another exec processing fields they could have known up front. This left avoidable model turns, tokens, and latency in common multi-operation workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trusted OpenClaw core and plugin tools can now declare an optional `outputSchema` for `AgentToolResult.details`. Code Mode and Tool Search expose a bounded TypeScript-style output hint only when that schema is complete and closed; open, oversized, unsupported, MCP, and client schemas remain unknown and raw-first.

OpenClaw compiles trusted output schemas before execution, then validates final details after normal hooks. The compact renderer has strict depth/property/character/union bounds. Remote and client schemas stay deferred as `input: "unknown"` and use object identity for catalog reuse, preventing attacker-sized metadata walks while preserving schema-replacement invalidation. `agents_list` adopts the contract as the first built-in example.

The change also promotes Code Mode to a dedicated `/tools/code-mode` documentation page with Quickstart, runtime semantics, guest API, output-contract authoring, trust/validation rules, fallback behavior, debugging, and validation guidance. The old `/reference/code-mode` route redirects to it.

## User Impact

Code Mode can call and process tools with declared result shapes in the first exec instead of paying a raw-inspection round trip. Unknown outputs keep the safe existing raw-first behavior. Plugin authors get one documented result contract shared by Tool Search and Code Mode, without trusting remote MCP or client schema claims.

## Evidence

Live multi-provider matrix: four validated Code Mode tasks per provider over the real Agent runtime and a 72-tool catalog with adversarial decoys. Baseline is merged #109651; after is this branch.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Validated tasks | 11/12 | 12/12 | +1 |
| Model turns | 29 | 26 | -10% |
| Code Mode exec calls | 17 | 14 | -18% |
| Decoy calls | 0 | 0 | unchanged |
| Total latency | 81.4s | 70.4s | -13% |
| Input tokens | 38,827 | 36,025 | -7% |
| Output tokens | 2,388 | 2,380 | unchanged |

Stress: three complete Code Mode matrices produced 34/36 validated tasks, 78 turns, 42 exec calls, 57 underlying service calls, and zero decoy calls. Anthropic and Google were 12/12; OpenAI was 10/12. Both misses were the model filtering singular fixture value `plum` with the plural word `plums` after selecting the correct real tool, not a discovery, transport, schema, or decoy failure. A final OpenAI/Google pass kept every completed task at two turns and one exec. The final Anthropic retry hit provider overload before tokens or tools; earlier Anthropic stress was 12/12.

Validation:

- Exact final head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/code-mode.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts src/agents/tool-schema-hints.test.ts` — 142 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox: 250 focused tests passed; all changed gates passed, including core/plugin/test/script typechecks, full lint, SDK API/surface/boundary checks, and the full production build.
- Adversarial regressions cover malformed schemas before side effects, post-hook result validation, schema replacement, closed/truncated/unsupported shapes, huge keys/catalogs, untrusted client/MCP schema deferral, and zero traversal of hostile schema proxies.
- Source-blind behavior contract: satisfied at 0.86 confidence; all seven clauses passed, including state-changing irrigation, missing-tool recovery, zero decoys, provider-error classification, and docs navigation/redirect behavior.

target.title: fix(update): prevent compatible plugins from being skipped after npm-global upgrades
target.body:
Refs #93908

## Summary

- Pin current-process post-core plugin compatibility checks to the installed target OpenClaw version for upgrades as well as downgrades.
- Pass that installed target version into mandatory post-core plugin convergence instead of overwriting the compatibility context with the stale updater-process `VERSION`.
- Preserve current `main`'s ClawHub risk-acknowledgement plumbing while keeping the installed target as the compatibility source of truth.
- Add focused regression coverage for the reported `2026.5.28` → `2026.6.8` Feishu/plugin API compatibility path.

## What Problem This Solves

An npm-global update replaces the installed OpenClaw package before the updater process exits. During that window, post-core plugin convergence can evaluate retained plugins against the updater's stale pre-update `VERSION` instead of the installed target version. A plugin that is compatible with the target gateway can therefore be skipped before restart. This patch makes the update handoff use the installed target version consistently, matching the host that will own the plugin after restart.

## User Impact

After an npm-global core update, the still-running updater process can report its pre-update version while the installed package and the gateway that will restart are already newer. A retained plugin compatible with the installed target can therefore be rejected during post-core convergence. In the reported path, Feishu `2026.6.8` is skipped as incompatible with stale host `2026.5.28`, leaving the channel unavailable even though core `2026.6.8` is installed.

This patch makes update-owned compatibility decisions use the installed target version that will run after restart. It does not relax compatibility ranges or add a Feishu-specific exception.

## Root Cause

Fresh post-core child processes already receive `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION=<installed target>`, but the current-process path previously pinned that value only for downgrades. Mandatory convergence also replaced inherited compatibility-host state with the updater module's stale `VERSION`.

The canonical source of truth during post-core update convergence is the installed target package version, because that is the host version that will own the plugin after restart. The patch passes that value through the existing compatibility resolver boundary and restores the caller's environment after the scoped phase.

If the installed target version cannot be read, convergence retains the existing fallback to runtime `VERSION`.

## What Did Not Change

- Feishu package metadata and `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` requirements.
- Semver compatibility enforcement or plugin manifest parsing.
- Default plugin installation policy or ClawHub trust/risk acknowledgement.
- Runtime behavior for genuinely incompatible plugins.
- General runtime host-version discovery outside the npm-global update handoff.

The last point is why this PR now uses `Refs #93908` rather than closing syntax: the issue also contains a distinct post-restart `unknown_host_version` reproduction that this update-scoped patch does not resolve.

## Evidence

### Real npm-global update and retained-plugin lifecycle

A disposable Windows environment used an isolated npm prefix, HOME, state directory, config and gateway port. `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` was unset for the actual update. No external Feishu credentials were used because the behavior under test is package compatibility, retention and discovery rather than network delivery.

1. Installed the real npm package `openclaw@2026.5.28` into the isolated global prefix:

   ```text
   OpenClaw 2026.5.28 (e932160)
   ```

2. Installed and retained the real npm plugin `@openclaw/feishu@2026.6.8`. With the compatibility override absent, the baseline production CLI reproduced the stale-host rejection:

   ```text
   plugin requires OpenClaw >=2026.5.29, but this host is 2026.5.28; skipping load
   ```

3. Ran the real production update command against a target `2026.6.8` package carrying this PR's emitted update-path changes:

   ```text
   openclaw update --yes --timeout 600
   ```

   The command performed the real managed-gateway stop and npm-global replacement:

   ```text
   Updating OpenClaw...
   Stopping managed gateway service before package update...

   Update Result: OK
     Before: 2026.5.28
     After:  2026.6.8

   Steps:
     ✓ global update
     ✓ global install swap
     ✓ openclaw doctor
   ```

4. The same current-process update then reached production post-core plugin convergence. It retained the compatible Feishu release instead of applying the stale `2026.5.28` host decision:

   ```text
   Resolved @openclaw/feishu to @openclaw/feishu@2026.6.11, but that version is incompatible with this OpenClaw runtime; using newest compatible @openclaw/feishu@2026.6.8.
   npm plugins: 0 updated, 1 unchanged.
   ```

5. After replacement, the real production service adapter restarted the gateway and handled a stale process:

   ```text
   Restarted Scheduled Task: OpenClaw PR95384 Proof
   Found stale gateway process(es): 22948.
   Stopping stale process(es) and retrying restart...
   Restarted Scheduled Task: OpenClaw PR95384 Proof
   ```

6. Authenticated production RPC health verified the replacement target:

   ```text
   cli.version:        2026.6.8
   gateway.version:    2026.6.8
   rpc.ok:             true
   rpc.server.version: 2026.6.8
   plugin drifts:      []
   ```

7. Post-restart production discovery retained and enabled the real npm plugin:

   ```text
   Feishu/Lark | feishu | enabled | ...\@openclaw\feishu\dist\index.js | 2026.6.8
   ```

### Proof boundary

The first `openclaw update` invocation completed package replacement and post-core plugin convergence, but the execution harness terminated it after approximately 606 seconds before its own restart phase. Restart, authenticated health and post-restart discovery were then completed through separate real production CLI invocations against the replaced install. This is not presented as one uninterrupted exit-0 update command.

The target artifact was synthesized from the published `openclaw@2026.6.8` production bundle with the PR's emitted update-path semantics because a full Windows repository build exhausted the available V8 heap near 8 GB. It exercised shipped production JavaScript, npm replacement, plugin convergence, the service adapter, gateway process, authenticated RPC and plugin discovery, but was not an official package built end-to-end from this exact PR head.

To avoid creating a machine-wide Scheduled Task, the production Windows service adapter used its per-user Startup/service-script fallback. The gateway child process, listener, restart, RPC version and plugin discovery were independently verified.

### Current-head regression verification

After syncing onto current `main`, head `7b5d246a91ebae47d53f67702da20cf499cd9953` passed:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/update-cli.test.ts -t "pins the compatibility host version"
2 passed, 180 skipped

pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts
22 passed

pnpm exec vitest run src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts -t "reports local audio acceleration as information without failing doctor health"
1 passed, 90 skipped

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
passed
```

The doctor test is included because the prior CI failure was outside this PR's diff and came from a stale base; current `main` already contains the corresponding doctor fix.

## Review Feedback Status

- The requested production evidence is substantially stronger but remains partially open: npm-global replacement and post-core convergence completed in the update invocation, while restart, authenticated health and retained-plugin discovery were verified through subsequent production CLI invocations rather than the same exit-0 update process.
- The package root moved from `2026.5.28` to `2026.6.8`; Feishu `2026.6.8` was retained during convergence; the restarted gateway and RPC reported `2026.6.8`; and post-restart discovery reported Feishu enabled. Because the target was a synthesized production bundle rather than a full build from this exact head, this is not claimed as complete current-head artifact proof.
- Closing syntax was replaced with `Refs #93908`; the broader runtime unknown-host-version reproduction remains outside this patch.
- No additional mechanical code defect was identified. The remaining maintainer decision is whether this disclosed split production lifecycle is sufficient or whether one uninterrupted managed-service update using an artifact fully built from the PR head is required.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` verifies that both upgrade and downgrade current-process paths expose the installed target compatibility version only during post-core plugin update and restore the previous environment afterward.
- `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts` verifies that explicit installed-target compatibility state reaches mandatory convergence instead of being replaced by stale in-process `VERSION`.
- Existing convergence fallback remains covered when no target version can be read.
- The production proof verifies the same source-of-truth handoff through real npm replacement, retained-plugin convergence and post-restart discovery.

The test fixture's `as unknown as OpenClawConfig` follows the pre-existing minimal-config test style; production code adds no type escape or disabled check.

## Merge Risk

Relevant surfaces are plugin availability, compatibility and the npm-global update lifecycle.

The change is narrow: only update-owned post-core compatibility checks use the installed target version. It does not change public config/schema/protocol, loosen plugin constraints, or introduce a new environment/config surface. Fresh post-core child processes already use this installed-target contract; this patch makes current-process convergence follow the same invariant and preserves the existing fallback when the target cannot be read.

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

```console
# Active descendant check: countActiveDescendantRuns() smoke test
$ node --import tsx -e "import { countActiveDescendantRuns } from './src/agents/subagent-registry-read.ts'; console.log('empty key:', countActiveDescendantRuns(''), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('unknown key:', countActiveDescendantRuns('no-such'), '(safe fallback)'); console.log('All returned 0 without throwing ✅');"
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn claude --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:claude:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests**: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed**
**Typecheck**: `pnpm check:test-types` — passed
**Build**: `pnpm build` — passed

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Cross-agent ACP spawn label persistence — label written to target agent's session store, resolved via `sessions.resolve` by label.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-spawn-label-106136`, binary `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`.

**Gateway** — started with acpx lazy backend, 12 plugins loaded:

```
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_ACPX_RUNTIME_PROBE=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair,
  file-transfer, memory-core, memory-wiki, minimax, phone-control, talk-voice; 3.4s)
gateway ready
```

**Cross-agent spawn** — `/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795` via Gateway WebSocket `chat.send` RPC, requester `main_assistant`, target `claude` (acpx backend):

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main",
     "message":"/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795",...}}
<<< {"runId":"proof-spawn-...","status":"started"}

[event] chat reply:
  ✅ Spawned ACP session agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3
  (persistent, backend acpx).
```

**Label resolution** — `sessions.resolve` by label via Gateway WebSocket:

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"sessions.resolve","params":{"label":"proof-1784006976795"}}
<<< {"ok":true,"key":"agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3"}
```

**Session list confirmation** — cross-agent session appears in list with correct label:

```
agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3 → label="proof-1784006976795"
# Owner is "claude" — cross-agent confirmed ✓
```

Observed result after fix:
- `/acp spawn claude --label` → session created as `agent:claude:acp:…` in target (claude) store ✓
- `sessions.resolve({label})` → returns `agent:claude:acp:…` (cross-agent owner) ✓
- Before fix: label was written to `main_assistant` store → silently lost ✗

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{

    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Catalog-path coverage proves Tool Search / Code Mode preserves plugin result control.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

## Summary

When an adapter returns an empty provider.model, backfill it with the resolved model name from resolveProviderModel.

Memory embedding provider can return an empty provider.model string, causing downstream identity mismatch and broken vector search (#90042).

target.title: fix(approval): preserve Unicode in native-route approval slug truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When exec approval command IDs contain multi-byte Unicode characters near the 8-character slug boundary, raw `.slice(0, 8)` could split UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing garbled short codes in user-facing approval notices.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, matching the pattern already used in `src/logging/redact.ts` and `src/tui/tui-local-shell.ts`.

## User Impact

Approval fallback notices (`/approve <slug> <decisions>`) will display correct Unicode characters instead of potentially corrupted short codes.

## Evidence

- Same mechanical pattern as 18+ modules already fixed across the codebase
- `sliceUtf16Safe` is dependency-free and already imported in `src/`

target.title: fix: isolate coding-agent Codex CLI with dedicated CODEX_HOME
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who run the bundled `coding-agent` skill with Codex CLI against the ambient Codex home (`$CODEX_HOME` / `~/.codex`) while OpenClaw holds ChatGPT OAuth for the same account would hit persistent OpenClaw OAuth refresh failures (`refresh_token_reused` / login-expired guidance).

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill’s documented Codex launch form previously ran ambient `codex exec`, which can share and rotate ChatGPT refresh tokens with OpenClaw’s OAuth profile. This change makes a dedicated worker `CODEX_HOME` mandatory for Codex workers: one-time `codex login` into that home, `codex login status` preflight, and command-scoped `CODEX_HOME` only on Codex worker commands so OpenClaw remains the canonical OAuth owner. `CODEX_HOME_CODING_AGENT` selects a custom worker home consistently across setup, normal launches, and scratch launches; otherwise all three use `~/.codex-coding-agent`. No OpenClaw runtime auth APIs, provider plugins, or config knobs change.

The worker home is documented as a complete independent Codex profile, not only an auth directory. The upgrade guidance names the configuration/state that is not inherited and gives a safe migration path that never copies or links OAuth credentials.

Fix quality: compatibility — OpenClaw config/API remains unchanged, while the intentional Codex worker-profile reset and one-time setup are explicit; performance — none (static docs); usability — explicit setup + preflight instead of silent collision; security — keeps OpenClaw OAuth ownership separate from external worker credentials.

## User Impact

Operators who enable `coding-agent` and use Codex CLI get clear isolation instructions. Codex workers use `~/.codex-coding-agent` (or a dedicated path selected with `CODEX_HOME_CODING_AGENT`) so OpenClaw ChatGPT OAuth stays usable after worker launches. Existing users must complete one separate worker login once and selectively recreate any required non-secret Codex customization. Claude Code and OpenCode launch forms are unchanged.

## Compatibility and upgrade

A dedicated `CODEX_HOME` does not inherit the ambient Codex profile’s `config.toml`, profile overrides, MCP/plugin setup, skills or instructions, hooks, memories, logs, history, or sessions. The skill now tells users to:

1. start with an empty worker home and authenticate it separately;
2. never copy or symlink the ambient home, `auth.json`, `.credentials.json`, or keyring credentials;
3. recreate only required settings by reviewing and copying known non-secret files individually, configuring MCP servers under the worker home, and separately authorizing credential-bearing integrations;
4. leave logs, history, memories, and sessions behind because they are unnecessary and may contain sensitive context.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS. Docs/skill-only change.

```text
$ git diff --check
# clean

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check skills/coding-agent/SKILL.md docs/concepts/oauth.md
All matched files use the correct format.

$ pnpm docs:list
# completed successfully

$ .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.94)
```

Source inspection confirmed:

- both documented Codex launch forms scope `CODEX_HOME` to `${CODEX_HOME_CODING_AGENT:-$HOME/.codex-coding-agent}`;
- setup, login preflight, normal launches, and scratch launches resolve the same override/default;
- ambient `command:"codex exec ..."` guidance is gone;
- Claude Code and OpenCode forms remain unchanged;
- upstream Codex 0.144.4 resolves configuration and state from `CODEX_HOME`, stores file credentials at `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`, and keys platform credential storage by the selected home ([Codex config contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.144.4/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs#L4339-L4348), [credential storage contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.144.4/codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs#L231-L244)).

## Real behavior proof

The linked issue contains a redacted live recovery run on macOS 15.7.7 with OpenClaw 2026.7.1 and Codex CLI 0.144.4. After removing the ambient Codex credential from discovery, re-authenticating OpenClaw, and authorizing a separate worker-only `CODEX_HOME`:

```text
OpenClaw real openai/gpt-5.6-sol request: AUTH_OK
Codex worker real gpt-5.6-sol request: CODING_AGENT_AUTH_OK
openclaw models status: OAuth profile usable
CODEX_HOME=~/.codex-coding-agent codex login status: Logged in using ChatGPT
isolated auth.json: absent (credential stored in macOS Keychain)
```

That run used the same command-scoped dedicated-home behavior now documented by this patch. Account identifiers, tokens, absolute local paths, and device codes were omitted. Full reproduction, failure logs, environment, and recovery sequence are in #109704.

Current-main control: both coding-agent Codex launch forms used ambient `codex exec`, with no worker login, dedicated home, or preflight. This patch changes both launch forms and adds the required setup and migration contract.

The live recovery was captured for the issue before this documentation commit rather than repeated after the text-only patch. ClawSweeper’s review of `0ed6b9f6b` marked this evidence `proof: sufficient` for the documentation-only workflow change.

Fixes #109704

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok and Codex).

target.title: feat(feishu): bot-to-bot conversation support with @mention handling
target.body:
## Summary

Makes Feishu bot-to-bot conversations actually work. Bot-authored messages already reach dispatch on `main` (nothing gates them out), so bots could already "talk" — but the experience was broken: replies frequently never reached the peer bot because the `@mention` was missing or used the wrong syntax for the payload, so the conversation silently died. This PR makes bot-to-bot replies reliable — correct, payload-aware `@mention` delivery on every visible path (text, chunked, card, streaming) — and adds opt-in (`allowBots`) plus loop-protection controls. (In a Feishu group a message only notifies the entities it explicitly `@mentions`, so a reply without the right `@` is silently never delivered.)

- Continue treating incoming bot messages like user messages (now gated by an `allowBots` opt-in) so the agent can take part in bot-to-bot threads.
- New `bot-name` resolution module backed by the bot batch API as a weak dependency: falls back to the `open_id` when the bot info scope is absent.
- Per-chat mention registry resolving display name → `open_id` for outbound use.
- Outbound mention handling: teach `<at user_id="...">` syntax in the system prompt, strip only the leading self-mention, preserve + dedup other mentions, escape `<`/`>` in display names.
- Guarantee bot-to-bot replies `@mention` the bot sender via a deterministic `ensureMention` backstop, applied **per outbound unit** (every text chunk and the streaming-card close) using the **syntax that matches the payload** — `<at user_id="...">` for text/post messages, `<at id=...>` for lark_md cards — so the peer bot is notified on every visible path. Replies are delivered inline, not in a topic thread.
- `allowBots` opt-in (default: accept, preserving current behavior) lets operators set `false` to ignore bots or `"mentions"` to accept only when `@mentioned`.
- Shared bot-pair loop guard: bot-authored turns are wired into core `botLoopProtection` (sliding window, on by default) plus a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes.
- Core owns the group reply-delivery mode; the feishu `@mention` hint stays delivery-mode-agnostic (no duplicate delivery-mode computation in the plugin).

Aligns with #71396 — main no longer auto-prepends mentions, so this does not reintroduce the third-party mention cascade: the `mentionTargets` block stays context-only and never tells the model to re-`@` listed users.

Scope: changes are under `extensions/feishu/**` plus the feishu docs page. The one non-plugin file is `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts`, regenerated (`pnpm config:channels:gen`) because the new `allowBots`/`botLoopProtection` config fields must appear in the aggregated bundled-plugin config metadata that the config-metadata check validates.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu` — green, including the new/updated `outbound-mention`, `reply-dispatcher`, `bot` (bot-authored handling), and `monitor` suites covering card vs text mention syntax, per-chunk mentions, `allowBots` gating, and loop-guard suppression.
- `pnpm config:channels:gen --check`, `tsgo`, and `oxlint` clean for the touched surface.
- Real-machine verification in a live Feishu group (see proof below).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a group bot-to-bot reply now `@mentions` the bot sender so the other bot actually receives it — across text messages, chunked replies, and lark_md cards; replies to a human still `@` the human; a silent turn stays `NO_REPLY`. With `allowBots: false` the bot ignores other bots' messages. Previously a bot replying to a bot could omit the `@` (or use the wrong card syntax) and the reply was silently never delivered.

Real environment tested: a live Feishu group containing two bots and one human participant; the agent ran as one bot and replied across multiple turns to the other bot and to the human, under both text and card render modes, and with `allowBots` toggled. (Identifiers below are redacted.)

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran `pnpm config:channels:gen`, rebuilt and restarted the gateway, then drove a multi-turn bot-to-bot exchange in the live group; captured the agent session trajectory and compared it against the messages actually delivered to the group; toggled `allowBots` and a tight `botLoopProtection` window to observe gating.

Evidence after fix:

- On turns where the sender was the other bot, the inbound prompt carried `[System: "<name>" (open_id: ou_<bot-sender-redacted>) is a bot and receives your reply only if you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]`, and the reply led with the bot sender's `<at>` — the peer bot received it.
- `ensureMention` backstop verified live: on a turn where the raw model output omitted the bot sender's `@`, the message actually delivered to the group still contained it — the dispatcher backfilled it.
- Card path verified live: a reply rendered as a lark_md card carried the card mention syntax (`<at id=...>`) and the peer bot received it (the text-form tag would not have notified inside a card).
- `allowBots` verified live: with `allowBots` disabled, the peer bot's messages no longer triggered a reply.

Copied live output from the session (open_ids and names redacted):

```text
# Inbound prompt to the agent — sender is the other bot:
[System: "<bot>" (open_id: ou_REDACTED) is a bot and receives your reply only if
 you @mention it. You MUST @mention it in your reply.]

# Agent reply that turn, as delivered to the group — leads with the bot sender's <at>:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> 好，背景比较清晰，… (reply continues)

# A later turn whose raw model output dropped the bot-sender @ (it only @'d the
# human). The message ACTUALLY delivered to the group still carried it — the
# dispatcher's ensureMention backfilled the bot sender before sending:
<at user_id="ou_REDACTED"><bot></at> <at user_id="ou_REDACTED_HUMAN"><human></at> 面试结论：…
```

Observed result after fix: the other bot received and continued the conversation across turns under both text and card modes; no silent drop. `allowBots: false` cleanly suppressed bot-authored replies. Replies addressed exactly the intended target and stayed inline.

What was not tested: the `message_tool` visible-reply path does not receive the deterministic backstop by design (see Design notes); that is an intentional product decision, not an untested gap.

## Design notes

- **Per-payload mention syntax.** Feishu uses two `<at>` forms: `<at user_id="...">Name</at>` for text/post messages and `<at id=...></at>` for lark_md cards. The backstop emits the form matching each outbound unit and re-applies it per chunk and on streaming-card close, so a long or card-rendered bot-to-bot reply notifies the peer on every message.
- **The deterministic backstop is intentionally scoped to the `automatic` reply path, not `message_tool`.** `automatic` is an implicit reply where the agent does not directly control delivery, so the dispatcher guarantees the bot-sender `@`. The `message_tool` path (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`) is an explicit, flexible send where the agent deliberately authors the message, recipients, and mentions; the plugin respects what the agent wrote and does **not** auto-inject — forcing one would override an intentional, author-controlled send. Outbound mention normalization still runs on both paths, so any `@` the agent does write is resolved correctly.
- **Bot-pair loop protection.** Bot-authored messages already reached dispatch on `main` (no gate drops them), so the bot-pair possibility is not introduced here. This PR adds the safety: `allowBots` (default accept; `false`/`"mentions"` to restrict), a Layer-1 self-filter that drops the bot's own webhook echoes, and wiring of accepted bot-authored turns into core's shared `botLoopProtection` sliding-window guard (on by default). Tunable/disable-able via `channels.feishu.botLoopProtection`.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

Cyber:

```text
Config valid: /home/umbrel/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Gateway ready after restart
Health: Discord configured, Telegram configured, WhatsApp linked
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/embedded-agent-Cv8lGIPa.js: createEmbeddedHookSessionResetQueue present
/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/run-session-target-D5j70_wT.js: buildCompactionHookApi present
```

Sovereign:

```text
Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
```

Provider error bodies containing emoji or other multi-byte Unicode characters at the 4000-character truncation boundary would produce lone surrogate code units (mojibake) in user-visible error messages.
