target.title: fix(xai): add handshakeTimeout to TTS stream WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI TTS stream creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The existing `connectTimer` fires after `timeoutMs` and calls `failConnect()`, which **rejects the promise but does not close or terminate the WebSocket** — the underlying TCP connection and its memory remain occupied. The `handshakeTimeout` at the ws library level cleans up the TCP connection when the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade stalls.

The voice bridge was excluded: its `connectTimeout` already calls `ws.terminate()`, which the pinned ws library aborts the active request and destroys the socket even in CONNECTING state.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: timeoutMs` (30 s default) — passes the existing timeout parameter to the ws constructor so the library itself enforces the upgrade deadline and releases TCP resources.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS connections now release TCP resources within their configured timeout instead of leaking them until GC. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER (5 s)","handshakeTimeoutMs":5000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":5015}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally).
- **AFTER**: `"Opening handshake has timed out"` at 5015 ms — terminated within deadline.

### Why only TTS (not voice bridge)

| Function | Existing timeout mechanism | Cleans up TCP? | handshakeTimeout needed? |
|------|------|------|------|
| `xaiTTSStream` | `connectTimer → failConnect()` | **No** — only rejects promise | ✅ Yes |
| `XaiRealtimeVoiceBridge` | `connectTimeout → ws.terminate()` | Yes — terminate() destroys socket | ❌ No (reverted) |

### Focused tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/tts.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  26 passed (26)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  36 passed (36)

target.body:
@
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Rebase Note

Rebased onto current main (9ddd988c9) to pick up the rename `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout`. The private helper `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` is now re-exported for direct testing.

## What Changed (vs previous revision)

- **Rebased onto main**: Resolved merge conflicts with the `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` rename and added test for stalled DNS preflight.
- **Re-exported `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo`**: The function was un-exported during the main rename; re-exported so bounded-read tests can target it directly.
- **Fixed lint**: Added curly braces to `if (res.destroyed) return;` one-liners in the test (eslint `curly`).

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

**Non-transient overflow:** Size overflow now throws as non-transient (`transient: false`) so the detail message propagates to callers instead of being swallowed by the generic "fetch failed" wrapper.

## Evidence

### 1. Static / focused tests

target.body: ## Summary - Register Feishu `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1` in the bundled `feishu` monitor dispatcher. - Convert valid VC meeting invite events into synthetic inbound Feishu direct-message turns from the inviter, reusing the existing DM pairing, allowlist, dynamic agent creation, session recording, and reply-dispatch path. - Ask the agent to join immediately by meeting number, with instructions to pass `call_id` only when the installed join tool exposes that parameter. - Route follow-up replies to the real Feishu inviter target (`user:` / `user:`), not a synthetic meeting route, so the normal `message` tool and final replies stay on the supported Feishu DM channel. - Document the required `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1` event subscription for meeting invite auto-join. ## Linked context Fixes #91677. Supersedes #89751 with the same final behavior on a clean single-commit branch. This PR is based on the Feishu VC meeting invite behavior tested from live bot invitations and the sibling Feishu invite flow. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Feishu VC bot meeting invite events now reach OpenClaw through the bundled `feishu` plugin and trigger an immediate meeting-join turn while preserving the normal Feishu reply/session route back to the inviter. Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw gateway using the linked bundled `extensions/feishu` plugin, with a live Feishu bot and live VC meeting invitations. Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built and installed the OpenClaw branch locally, verified the gateway was loading `openclaw` rather than the older external `openclaw-lark` plugin, restarted the gateway after rebuilding, sent live Feishu VC meeting invitations to the bot, inspected gateway/runtime logs and agent tool invocations, then reran the focused validation commands listed below. Evidence after fix: Runtime logs showed `feishu[default]: vc meeting invited, dispatching synthetic inbound` for live meeting invites. The join path invoked `lark-cli vc +meeting-join --meeting-number ... --format json`; one invalid meeting returned Feishu code `121005` (`meeting not exist`), and a later live invite joined successfully with a meeting number, meeting id, start time, and topic returned by Feishu. Focused tests assert the finalized inbound context uses `To` and `OriginatingTo` as the inviter's supported Feishu DM target, creates a Feishu reply dispatcher for that target, and does not call the removed direct acknowledgement send path for dispatched invites. Observed result after fix: The live Feishu invite event was accepted by the `feishu` plugin, converted into a synthetic inbound turn, joined the meeting by meeting number, and kept follow-up agent replies on the inviter's standard Feishu direct-message route instead of `vc-meeting:`. What was not tested: I did not attach screenshots or sanitized transcript artifacts to the PR. The live validation used local gateway logs and Feishu runtime/tool output rather than a published artifact. Proof limitations or environment constraints: The real-environment proof depends on a live Feishu bot, live meeting invite, and local gateway configuration. The PR therefore includes focused regression tests for the dispatch, dedupe, reply target, pairing-blocked, user_id-only pairing, and compatibility branches so the behavior remains reviewable without access to that live Feishu environment. ## Tests and validation - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/monitor.vc-meeting-invited-handler.test.ts` - `pnpm check:test-types` - `node scripts/run-bundled-extension-oxlint.mjs` - `git diff --check` - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings ## Risk checklist - User-visible behavior: yes. A Feishu VC invite to the bot can now create an inbound turn that attempts to join the meeting. - Configuration/operator action: yes. Feishu apps must subscribe to `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1`; the docs were updated with that event. - Message delivery/session routing: covered. Invite-triggered replies use the real inviter DM target and avoid persisting a synthetic `vc-meeting:*` last-route target. - Tool compatibility: covered. The prompt instructs the agent to use `call_id` only when the available join tool supports it, keeping older `lark-cli` versions usable. - Security/privacy: no new credentials or persisted secrets. The handler keeps invite context limited to the fields needed for joining and reply routing. - Rollback: disable the Feishu event subscription or the bundled `feishu` channel/plugin to stop invite-triggered turns. ## Reviewer focus The remaining product decision is whether Feishu event subscription is sufficient opt-in for automatic meeting-join turns, or whether maintainers prefer an additional default-off Feishu config gate before merge.

target.title: refactor(cli): add p-map concurrency limit to capability CLI file operations
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. On large batches (100+ files), this causes simultaneous file reads, image conversions, downloads, and inference requests at once - risking EMFILE exhaustion, OOM from buffering many image buffers simultaneously, connection-pool starvation for provider API calls, and CPU overcommit from parallel sharp image processing.

**Solution**: Replace 5 `Promise.all(x.map(async ...))` calls with `pMap(x, ..., { concurrency: 20 })`. p-map v7.0.5 is already a direct dependency used across 7+ other modules in the codebase including media-understanding, cron, and gateway server startup. No new dependencies introduced.

**What changed**: 5 async mapping locations in `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`. Each function's core logic and error handling remain unchanged - only the outer iteration over the dynamic array is bounded. The inner `Promise.all` calls within each iteration (e.g., per-image metadata gathering) continue to run in parallel as a fixed-size batch within one pMap slot.

**What did NOT change**: Inner per-item `Promise.all` calls, error handling, return types, function signatures, behavior for single or small-batch invocations. Zero behavioral change at the small scale covered by existing unit tests.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
`capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. On large batches (100+ files), this causes simultaneous file reads, image conversions, downloads, and inference requests at once - risking EMFILE exhaustion, OOM from buffering many image buffers simultaneously, connection-pool starvation for provider API calls, and CPU overcommit from parallel sharp image processing.

**Root Cause**:
`capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. target.title: feat(write): add capability-gated native append
target.body:
## Summary

Adds capability-gated native append support to the built-in `write` tool for #40001.

- `append: true` is opt-in and appears only when the active backend supports it.
- Docker-style and remote-shell sandboxes use a pinned `O_APPEND` mutation rather than read-modify-write.
- OpenShell remains unsupported because its mirror-sync architecture cannot provide authoritative-target append semantics.
- Unacknowledged append outcomes are fail-closed and explicitly must not be retried automatically.
- The optional Plugin SDK bridge capability and baseline are updated.

## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent writers could lose data when append was emulated by reading the whole file and overwriting it with old content plus a suffix. This change gives supported sandbox backends a native append path so independent writers do not overwrite already-persisted content.

## Lineage

This is a fresh current-main successor to closed PRs #77127 and #102243. The latter was closed after review identified that a safe sandbox implementation required a native `SandboxFsBridge.appendFile` primitive; this candidate implements that boundary instead of preserving the sandbox read-modify-write path. A fresh issue/title/head search found no open append candidate for #40001.

## Evidence

**Real setup tested**

An isolated Docker container with networking disabled and a bind-mounted temporary workspace, exercised through the actual `SandboxFsBridge` and `docker exec` transport. No live gateway or production state was used.

**Current-head validation**

- Final candidate head: `056f4763ab9becd41f1ed0afe86389c76fa1bf84`, rebased onto `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`.
- All 10 changed test files passed: 153 tests across the agent and OpenShell Vitest shards.
- Core and extension source/test type gates passed on the final head.
- Plugin SDK API baseline and public surface checks passed; public wildcard reexports remained at 209.
- Full scripts lint, Control UI i18n, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The isolated Docker proof passed binary append, create-on-missing, two concurrent 128 KiB writers, restrictive `0600` creation mode, and read-only bind rejection without mutation. The append runtime blobs were verified unchanged by the subsequent base-only rebases.

**Observed result**

Supported sandbox backends append at EOF without a userspace read-modify-write cycle, and both independent writer payloads survived in the tested local-filesystem path.

**What was not tested**

- Network-filesystem append guarantees were not claimed or tested.
- OpenShell append remains intentionally unsupported.
- Append is not claimed to provide a transactional record boundary after a kernel short write.
- No idempotency key is provided; uncertain outcomes must not be automatically retried.

## Safety details

The pinned helper uses anchored directory traversal, `O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, pre/post-open regular-file checks, hardlink rejection, full first write with EINTR/short-write completion, and file/parent fsync. Append bypasses overwrite prechecks and uses backend acknowledgement as the only success signal.

Addresses #40001.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): treat blank env API keys as unconfigured
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `XI_API_KEY` environment values are truthy strings, so the ElevenLabs providers treated them as real credentials:

- `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured` returned `true` when `XI_API_KEY="  "`, so auto-selection could pick the realtime provider and only fail later at connection time.
- `transcribeElevenLabsAudio` skipped its `ElevenLabs API key missing` guard and sent the speech-to-text request with an empty `xi-api-key` header, surfacing as a confusing upstream 401 instead of a clear local configuration error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-file key path already normalizes blanks (`normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`), and the profile fallback already trims (`resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`). Only the raw env fallbacks bypassed normalization. This routes them (plus the request-level key, matching the merged xAI handling in `realtime-transcription-provider.ts`) through the same shared `normalizeOptionalString` helper so blank values are treated as missing everywhere in this provider.

## Changes

- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`: `isConfigured` and `createSession` resolve the `XI_API_KEY` fallback via `normalizeOptionalString`, so whitespace-only values report unconfigured and session creation fails fast with `ElevenLabs API key missing`.
- `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`: the speech-to-text key resolution normalizes `req.apiKey`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `XI_API_KEY` with the same helper, so blank values are skipped and env keys are trimmed before being sent.
- Regression tests: whitespace-only env keys are treated as missing in both providers (including asserting no request is sent), and a padded env key is trimmed before use.

## User Impact

Operators with a whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`XI_API_KEY` (e.g., a placeholder left in an env file) now get a clear "ElevenLabs API key missing" error and the realtime provider correctly reports itself unconfigured, instead of a request sent with an empty credential that fails upstream. Real keys are unaffected (verified trimmed-to-same-value in tests). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/` — 38/38 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in changed files (only pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors from a stale local dependency install).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Real HTTP proof below: loopback server + production functions, before/after this patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A whitespace-only `XI_API_KEY` made the realtime provider report configured, and the speech-to-text path sent a real request carrying an empty `xi-api-key` header instead of failing fast locally.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production functions imported directly from the changed sources, real `node:http` loopback server as the ElevenLabs API endpoint (`request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` to permit the loopback target). Current head: `446eea15d5535b6f0c64b2dca9c6d01047f43bac`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/elk-proof/proof.mts` with `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=""` and `XI_API_KEY="  "` in the environment. The driver starts a real HTTP server, calls `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured({ providerConfig: {} })`, then calls the production `transcribeElevenLabsAudio({ buffer, fileName, mime, baseUrl: <loopback>, request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true } })` and reads the server's received-request count and captured `xi-api-key` header back.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): true`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: resolved (request was sent)`, `server received requests: 1`, `captured xi-api-key header: ""`. After the patch: `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): false`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: threw: ElevenLabs API key missing`, `server received requests: 0`.

**Observed result after fix:** The whitespace-only env key no longer counts as configured, the missing-key error fires locally before any network I/O (the loopback server confirms zero requests), and regression tests confirm a padded real env key (`"  env-key  "`) is trimmed and sent as `env-key`.

**What was not tested:** No live ElevenLabs API calls (no real credential available); the loopback server stands in for the upstream endpoint. The realtime websocket session path was not connected end-to-end with a blank key; its `isConfigured`/`createSession` gates are covered by the new unit tests and the same normalization helper. No UI changes.

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other providers' env credential paths (bedrock was handled in #109680, `packages/ai` env keys in #109691, deepgram in #108565); this PR is scoped to ElevenLabs only.
- The config-file `apiKey` handling, which already normalizes blanks via `normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`.
- `resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`, which already trims its env read.

target.title: fix(skills): filter NaN from Date.parse in history scan session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resumePendingForBatchScan` in `src/skills/workshop/history-scan.ts` built session cursors by calling `Date.parse(session.updatedAt)` without filtering out `NaN`. When a session's `updatedAt` is missing, malformed, or otherwise not parseable, `updatedAtMs` became `NaN`, which then propagated through the resume cursor into subsequent scan iterations.

Filter `sessionCursors` so any entry whose `updatedAtMs` is not a finite number is dropped before it can reach the resume cursor. This preserves existing behavior for valid timestamps while ensuring malformed ones cannot poison the resume state.

target.title: fix(agents): agent-created files get lowercased names on Windows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, files and directories an agent creates get **lowercased names**. Ask for
`src/Components/MyComponent.tsx` and what lands on disk is `src\components\mycomponent.tsx`.

NTFS is case-insensitive but case-*preserving*, so nothing fails locally — the agent reads its own file
back fine. The damage shows up downstream: git records the lowercased name, and the TypeScript/React
import the agent just wrote (`./Components/MyComponent`) resolves on the author's Windows box but breaks
for every teammate on Linux/macOS and in CI. Any agent-authored name that is not already lowercase is
affected: `README.md`, `Dockerfile`, `MyClass.ts`.

For some names it is worse than a case change. `"İstanbul.md".toLowerCase()` is `"i̇stanbul.md"` —
U+0130 becomes the two code points U+0069 U+0307, one longer than the original and not reversible. So a
Turkish filename does not come back lowercased, it comes back **corrupted**.

This is Windows-only. The POSIX branch of the same function preserves case correctly today.

## Why This Change Was Made

`toRelativePathUnderRoot` (`src/agents/path-policy.ts:76-90`) ran both root and candidate through
`normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` and then **returned** the resulting relative path:

```ts
const rootForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(rootResolved);
const targetForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(resolvedCandidate);
const relative = path.win32.relative(rootForCompare, targetForCompare);
return validateRelativePathWithinBoundary({ relativePath: relative, ... });
```

That helper lowercases (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1`, `dist/path.js:17` →
`normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...)`). Lowercasing is right for a **comparison key** — which is exactly
how the other two call sites use it — but this function hands the relative path back to callers, and they
build files out of it:

- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1089-1092` — `mkdir`: `path.resolve(root, relative)` → `fs.mkdir`
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1059-1060` — `writeWorkspaceFile` → `.write(relative, { mkdir: true })`
- `src/agents/apply-patch.ts:310,318,326` — `apply_patch` writeFile / remove / mkdirp

`toCanonicalRelativeWorkspacePath` (`agent-tools.read.ts:1167-1179`) does not rescue it: `fs.realpath`
restores the true case only of the **already-existing** ancestor, the new basename stays lowercased, and
line 1179 re-lowercases the whole thing on the way out. `assertSandboxPath` does not either — it is
handed the already-derived `resolved` path, not the original candidate.

The lowercasing was also never needed for the boundary math. `path.win32.relative` already matches the
root case-insensitively **and** returns the tail in its original case, so the pre-lowercasing bought
nothing and cost the filename. The one part of that normalization the boundary check does rely on is
extended-length prefix stripping — without it a `\\?\C:\...` candidate relativizes to
`..\..\..\?\C:\...` and gets rejected as an escape. So this adds `normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase`
next to the comparison variant in `src/infra/path-guards.ts`. It mirrors that helper step for step —
including the trim — minus the lowercasing, and a test pins that equivalence directly so the two cannot
drift:

```ts
expect(normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase(input).toLowerCase()).toBe(
  normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(input),
);
```

### Sibling surfaces

All three callers of `normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` were checked. Only this one was misusing it:

| Call site | Uses result as | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts:215` | comparison key (`===`) | correct, untouched |
| `isPathInside` (fs-safe) | discards relative, returns boolean | correct, untouched |
| `src/agents/path-policy.ts` | **returns it to callers** | fixed here |

## Evidence

**Live before/after on real Windows** (Windows 11, NTFS, Turkish locale), driving the real
`toRelativeWorkspacePath` through the exact call pattern of `agent-tools.read.ts`, then reading the names
back with `fs.readdirSync`:

Before (`origin/main`):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\components\mycomponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> components/mycomponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md  | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : i̇stanbul.md | length 12 | U+0069 U+0307
  identical? NO  <- filename corrupted, not just lowercased
```

After (this branch):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\Components\MyComponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> Components/MyComponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130 U+0073
  identical? YES
```

**Why the existing test did not catch it:** `path-policy.test.ts:23` used an all-lowercase candidate
(`c:/users/user/openclaw/memory/log.txt`), which passes either way. The new cases use mixed case.

**Tests** — every added mixed-case assertion fails on `origin/main` and passes here:

```
path-policy.test.ts + path-guards.test.ts        41/41 passed
+ agent-tools.workspace-paths, apply-patch,
  installed-plugin-index-record-reader            111 passed | 12 skipped, 0 failed
max-lines ratchet                                 OK
dead-export ratchet (knip)                        0 entries
oxlint / oxfmt --check                            clean
tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json                        no errors in touched files
```

## Merge Risk

Low, but this touches a sandbox boundary, so here is the containment argument explicitly.

**The boundary decision is unchanged.** `path.win32.relative` compares case-insensitively, so
`relative(lower(a), lower(b))` and `relative(a, b)` return the same *structure* — same number of `..`
segments, same segment count, same absoluteness. Only the case of the returned characters differs.
`validateRelativePathWithinBoundary` looks at exactly that structure (`""`/`"."`, `".."`, `"../"`,
`"..\\"`, `isAbsolute`), so every accept/reject verdict is identical. Verified empirically:

```
root: C:\Users\User\OpenClaw
escape, no lowercasing        -> "..\Other\log.txt"     still rejected
root itself, differing case   -> ""                     allowRoot still honored
drive-letter case c: vs C:    -> "Memory\Log.txt"       still matched
\\?\ prefix NOT stripped      -> "..\..\..\?\C:\..."    why stripping is kept
```

Two of the added tests pin this directly — an escape that differs from the root only by case is still
rejected, and a differently-cased root still resolves to `""` under `allowRoot`. Both pass before and
after the change, which is the point.

Scope is one file's Windows branch plus one new helper with a single caller. POSIX behavior is untouched.

target.title: fix(compaction): previous summary is duplicated when a later split degrades
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When staged compaction summarizes a long session and any split degrades, the previous summary is added
to the new summary **twice**. It then compounds: every later compaction cycle that has a degraded split
re-adds it again, so the summary grows a copy of itself each round and burns tokens on every subsequent
turn.

Since #86900 landed the staged circuit breaker to *stop* token burn when the summarizer is unavailable,
this is the same failure mode arriving through the merge path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`summarizeInStages` (`src/agents/compaction.ts:492`) stamped the merged result as a fallback if **any**
split degraded:

```ts
usedGenericFallback ||= result.kind === "generic-fallback";   // coarse OR over every chunk
...
return usedGenericFallback && mergedResult.kind === "summary"
  ? { kind: "generic-fallback", text: mergedResult.text }
  : mergedResult;
```

The only consumer of that kind is `summarizeViaLLM` (`src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts:413-420`),
which reads it to decide whether to restore the previous summary:

```ts
if (result.kind === "summary") {
  return result.text;
}
// A generic fallback means redistillation never happened. Preserve the
// known summary verbatim so a temporary model outage cannot erase it.
const previousSummary = params.previousSummary?.trim();
return previousSummary ? `${previousSummary}\n\n${result.text}` : result.text;
```

**That comment states an invariant the code does not hold.** The same function prepends the previous
summary as the *first message* (`:396-399` → `prependPreviousSummaryForRedistill`, `:107`), so it always
lands in chunk 0. If chunk 0 summarizes fine and a *later* chunk degrades, redistillation demonstrably
did happen — the merge already carries the summary — but the coarse flag stamps the result as a fallback
anyway, and the previous summary gets prepended on top of a merge that already contains it.

| oldest split | previous summary | correct | before |
|---|---|---|---|
| degraded | lost | restore it | restore ✔ |
| survived, later split degraded | **already in the merge** | **do not restore** | **restore again ✘** |

Reachable on the normal path: `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_GENERIC_FALLBACKS` (`:48`) only opens the circuit on
*consecutive* degradations, so a single failed split completes the merge, and `compaction-safeguard.ts:1375`
passes `previousSummary` on every repeat compaction.

The fix reports what the consumer actually asks — did the oldest split degrade — instead of "did anything
degrade". The coarse flag is removed rather than kept beside the precise one, so there is one source of
truth and the two cannot drift apart. With this, the existing comment becomes true.

Nothing outside these two modules reads the kind, so no other surface is affected. `compaction-safeguard.ts`
needs no change: its logic was already correct given a correct kind.

## Evidence

**End-to-end**, composing the real `summarizeInStages` with the verbatim decision from
`summarizeViaLLM:413-420`, with chunk 0 succeeding and a later chunk degrading:

Before (`origin/main`):

```
summarizeInStages kind : generic-fallback
final summary          : "## Goal\nShip the parser rewrite.\n\nmerged: ## Goal\nShip the parser rewrite. + newest"
previous summary occurs: 2 time(s)
```

After (this branch):

```
summarizeInStages kind : summary
final summary          : "merged: ## Goal\nShip the parser rewrite. + newest"
previous summary occurs: 1 time(s)
```

**Tests**

The added case (`oldest summary` → degraded → `newest summary` → merge) fails on `origin/main` with
`expected { kind: 'generic-fallback' } to deeply equal { kind: 'summary' }`, and passes here.

The existing `remains degraded` case is **unmodified and still green** — its oldest split is the one that
rejects, so the previous summary really is lost there and the fallback stamp is still correct. That is the
behavior split this change is built around.

```
compaction.circuit-breaker + compaction-safeguard + compaction-instructions   261 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed
all src/agents/compaction*.test.ts                                            103 passed | 14 skipped, 0 failed
max-lines ratchet                                                             OK
dead-export ratchet (knip)                                                    0 entries
oxlint / oxfmt --check                                                        clean
tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json                                                    no errors in touched files
```

`compaction-planning-worker.test.ts` fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` in this environment
(`Cannot find module compaction-planning.js` — the worker wants built output), so it is unrelated to this
change.

## Merge Risk

Low. One flag in one function, +14/-4 in source, no signature or type change, no config surface.

The only behavior that moves is the case this fixes: a merged summary whose oldest split survived is now
reported as `summary` instead of `generic-fallback`. The degraded-oldest-split path — the one the existing
test pins — is untouched, so the outage protection that #86900 added still holds exactly where it matters.

AI-assisted.

This loads both inventories from the Gateway (`cron.list` + `skills.status`), mirroring the existing `system.info` loader, and renders real counts, a placeholder while loading/offline, or an unavailable label when the Gateway cannot serve those methods. ## What Problem This Solves Control UI Settings -> Simple -> Automations displayed misleading zero counts for scheduled tasks and installed skills even on healthy installations with real cron jobs and skills. Operators could not tell whether the Gateway genuinely had no automations or the counts were simply not loaded, which sent them to troubleshooting/configuration pages unnecessarily (issue #107852). ## Evidence Before: `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` built the automation card state as `cronJobCount: 0, skillCount: 0` (hardcoded), so the card could never show a non-zero value. After: the card loads real counts via `cron.list` (the `total` field) and `skills.status` (`skills.length`), using the same request-id race-guard + gateway-source-binding + unavailable-state pattern as the adjacent `system.info` loader (`loadSystemInfo`). Counts render real values, a `-` placeholder while loading/offline, or an `Unavailable` label when the Gateway cannot serve the methods. rendered output is asserted through the DOM). - Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js run ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts ui/src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts --reporter=dot` - Evidence after fix: vitest reports `2 passed (2) / 48 passed (48)`; new tests assert the rendered Automation rows show real counts (`3 scheduled tasks`, `5 skills installed`), a `-` placeholder before load, and `Unavailable` when the Gateway cannot serve the inventory. - Observed result after fix: the Automation rows no longer render a misleading `0`; they render the loaded count, a loading placeholder, or an unavailable label. - What was not tested: a live Gateway + browser session showing the populated card (no live Gateway available in this sandbox). - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Windows sandbox without a running OpenClaw Gateway; real behavior is covered by unit tests that render the actual `renderQuickSettings` output and exercise the real `loadQuickAutomation` code path with a fake Gateway client, plus `tsgo` type validation. before after ## Tests and validation - `npx oxlint ` - clean. - `vitest run quick.test.ts config-page.test.ts` - 2 files, 48 tests passed. - `tsgo:ui` and `tsgo:test:ui` - exit 0 (no type errors; `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` satisfied via optional chaining). New/updated tests: - `quick.test.ts`: three tests covering real counts, loading placeholder, and unavailable label. - `config-page.test.ts`: `supportsQuickAutomation` unit test + `loadQuickAutomation` loader test (counts + unavailable). What failed before this fix: the Automation card always rendered `0 scheduled tasks` / `0 skills installed`. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? target.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite startup falls back to the system `mount` command when `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unavailable. That synchronous probe had no deadline, so a stalled `mount` process could block state or plugin database initialization indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback probe now has a one-second hard timeout. If filesystem classification times out, SQLite conservatively uses rollback journaling instead of assuming WAL is safe. Existing behavior for successful mount classification and non-timeout probe failures is preserved.

## User Impact

Database-backed OpenClaw startup no longer waits indefinitely on a wedged mount probe. When the deadline is reached, startup continues with rollback journaling, avoiding both the hang and an unsafe WAL assumption for an unclassified network filesystem.

## Evidence

- Regression-first tests cover the missing timeout and the conservative timeout policy.
- Before: the production `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` path with an isolated stalled `mount` fixture exceeded a 4-second external guard (`exit_status=124`).
- After: the same production path returned in about 1.0 seconds, selected `journal_mode=delete`, and exited successfully.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts` on Node 24.15.0: 38 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts src/infra/sqlite-wal.test.ts`: passed.
- Type-aware oxlint and TypeScript checking for the affected files: passed.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: no actionable findings after the conservative rollback follow-up.

Not exercised: a real macOS/BSD host or a real network filesystem. The live proof used the production SQLite configuration call path with a test-only local command fixture.

target.title: fix: reject unsafe Mattermost API path segments
target.body:
Closes #98389

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost plugin REST calls could reach a different bearer-token endpoint when a dynamic path component contained relative, URL-normalized, or malformed percent-encoded segments.

The affected workflow is Mattermost channel operation through the plugin REST client. Operators expect post, user, and channel ids to select the intended Mattermost endpoint; unsafe path-shaped values should fail before the client attaches the bot token and calls fetch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost client now rejects unsafe API path segments at one shared URL-builder boundary before preparing authorization headers. The direct authenticated media-file download path reuses the same builder. The guard handles raw `.` / `..`, encoded dot segments, backslash separator normalization, URL parser TAB/CR/LF normalization, and malformed percent encoding.

Normal Mattermost paths and request bodies are unchanged. This PR does not alter token storage, account resolution, or Mattermost response handling.

## User Impact

Mattermost users and operators get safer fail-closed behavior for malformed or unexpected REST path inputs. Legitimate Mattermost plugin requests continue to use the same `/api/v4` endpoints.

## Evidence

Before/source proof:

- On current `main`, `buildMattermostApiUrl` appended the requested suffix to `/api/v4` without rejecting dot segments first.
- WHATWG URL parsing normalizes examples like `http://localhost:8065/api/v4/posts/../users/me` to `/api/v4/users/me`, so a path-shaped id can change the endpoint selected under the Mattermost bot token.

After-fix proof on this branch:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-resources.test.ts` — 44 tests passed.
- The media regression supplies raw, encoded, backslash, URL-control, and malformed paths and proves `saveRemoteMedia` receives no request.
- Type-aware targeted oxlint passed for the four touched files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh uncommitted and full-branch autoreview passes reported no accepted/actionable findings.

No live Mattermost credentials were used. The requested mocked transport proof exercises the production shared URL builder before either authenticated transport boundary.

target.title: fix(qqbot): align typing lifecycle with core TypingController
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

  Fixes an issue where QQ Bot C2C users would see the "typing…" indicator driven by a self-built interval timer
  (TypingKeepAlive) that started and stopped independently of the model's actual inference and reply dispatch state. The
  typing cue could drift out of sync with the real reply progress (running too long after the reply was sent, or
  stopping early during long tool calls), and the keep-alive loop had to be hand-stopped at every early-return and
  finally-block in the gateway, creating fragile stop-site bookkeeping.

  Resolves the mismatch by wiring QQ typing into the OpenClaw core TypingController lifecycle, the same seam Telegram
  uses, so typing start/stop is precise to model onReplyStart and dispatch-idle.

  ## Why This Change Was Made

  The self-built TypingKeepAlive duplicated the core typing lifecycle's interval/in-flight-suppression logic and
  required manual stop() calls scattered across gateway.ts and outbound-dispatch.ts. This replaces it with
  createChannelMessageReplyPipeline + TypingController (via typingCallbacks in dispatcherOptions), so the core
  controller owns start (onReplyStart), keepalive refresh, and cleanup (markRunComplete + markDispatchIdle).

  Key design decisions and non-goals:

  - QQ's distinct typing model is preserved: input_second=10 display window with a 5s refresh interval
    (keepaliveIntervalMs, explicitly set rather than the core's 3s default so consecutive ticks overlap seamlessly), and
    every typing tick still spends one of QQ's 5-per-msg_id passive-reply slots — unlike Telegram's budget-free
    heartbeat.

  - typing-callbacks.ts owns the QQ-specific per-tick send: claimMessageReply(msgId, 1) reserves one passive slot for
    the final text reply; when only the reserved slot remains, the tick falls back to a proactive input_notify without
    msg_id so it never starves the final reply. One token-refresh retry; maxConsecutiveFailures=3.

  - gateway.startTypingForEvent now sends only the early input_notify cue (mirroring Telegram's early typing cue) and
    returns refIdx for quote resolution — no keepalive loop.

  - InboundContext.typing field and all keepAlive.stop() call sites are removed; the core controller is the single stop
    signal.

  - Non-goal: changing the passive-reply budget (still 5/hour) or the proactive-fallback behavior in
    sender.ts/streaming-c2c.ts.

  ## User Impact

  QQ Bot C2C users now see a "typing…" indicator that starts precisely when the model begins generating and stops as
  soon as the reply is dispatched — no more lingering indicators after the message lands, and no premature cutoff during
  long tool-augmented replies. Long-running turns are also safer: typing can no longer accidentally consume the last
  passive-reply slot, so the final text reply always gets through (falling back to a proactive message only when the
  hourly budget is genuinely exhausted).

  For group/guild messages, behavior is unchanged (no typing indicator, as before).

  ## Evidence

  - Tests: 669 qqbot tests pass (81 files), including 9 new typing-callbacks.test.ts tests covering per-tick budget
    claim (reserve=1), proactive fallback when only the reserved slot remains, token-refresh retry, non-token-error no-
    retry, and 3 budget-protection tests proving the final reply's passive slot survives typing ticks (including a
    simulated in-flight residual tick).

  - Delivery-trace goldens: Regenerated all 5 goldens. The new wire recording shows the core controller firing
    input_notify on onReplyStart (one extra passive spend per C2C scenario) and keepalive ticks every 5s; budget-
    exhaustion.trace.jsonl now demonstrates the proactive fallback (typing ticks at at=15000/at=20000 send without
    msg_id once the passive budget is reserved-exhausted, and only the first of five message-tool replies keeps msg_id).
    EXPECTED_REPLY_BUDGET_REMAINING updated accordingly (streaming-happy-c2c: 3→2, media-interrupt: 1→0, budget-
    exhaustion: 0).

  - Static checks: tsgo typecheck clean (production tsconfig.extensions.json + tsconfig.extensions.test.json), oxlint
    clean, oxfmt applied, git diff --check clean.

  - Note: $autoreview could not run in this environment (Codex engine returned 401 Unauthorized against
    wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses — environment auth, not a code issue); validation was completed via the test suite
    + typecheck/lint/format above.

Related: #109657

AI-assisted maintainer change. The implementation and final merged-tree behavior were manually reviewed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the LINE ingress path where a webhook could be acknowledged with HTTP 200 before detached event processing had durably completed, allowing a gateway crash or dispatch failure to silently lose inbound messages. The interim LINE-private worker also duplicated claim, retry, dead-letter, and adoption behavior now owned by the shared channel ingress drain.

## Why This Change Was Made

LINE now writes each raw webhook event to the shared SQLite ingress queue before acknowledgment and dispatches it through the core durable ingress drain. The adapter preserves per-source lane ordering, adopts the shared turn lifecycle, retains the prior per-spool eight-delivery concurrency cap across repeated timer pumps, and uses typed terminal failures while deleting the redundant replay-guard path. Completion tombstones use message IDs for messages and retain 30 days / 4,096 entries, strictly covering the removed guard's 10 minute / 4,096-entry window even when LINE changes `webhookEventId` on redelivery.

## User Impact

Accepted LINE events survive gateway restarts and transient dispatch failures, while duplicate redeliveries remain suppressed. Enqueue failure prevents the HTTP 200 acknowledgment so LINE can retry. No new configuration or public plugin API is introduced, and the core-drain adoption removes 252 net production lines.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line`: 30 files, 381 tests passed on the exact rebased head.
- Source-blind focused behavior validation: 10/10 spool scenarios passed, including no acknowledgment on enqueue failure, restart recovery, completion-tombstone rejection, changed-`webhookEventId` guard parity, raw-event persistence, retry, authentication dead-letter, no retry after committed delivery side effects, and the eight-delivery cap across repeated drain pumps.

target.title: fix(xai): add handshakeTimeout to TTS stream WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI TTS stream creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The existing `connectTimer` fires after `timeoutMs` and calls `failConnect()`, which **rejects the promise but does not close or terminate the WebSocket** — the underlying TCP connection and its memory remain occupied. The `handshakeTimeout` at the ws library level cleans up the TCP connection when the HTTP→WebSocket upgrade stalls.

The voice bridge was excluded: its `connectTimeout` already calls `ws.terminate()`, which the pinned ws library aborts the active request and destroys the socket even in CONNECTING state.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: timeoutMs` (30 s default) — passes the existing timeout parameter to the ws constructor so the library itself enforces the upgrade deadline and releases TCP resources.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI TTS connections now release TCP resources within their configured timeout instead of leaking them until GC. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER (5 s)","handshakeTimeoutMs":5000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":5015}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally).
- **AFTER**: `"Opening handshake has timed out"` at 5015 ms — terminated within deadline.

### Why only TTS (not voice bridge)

| Function | Existing timeout mechanism | Cleans up TCP? | handshakeTimeout needed? |
|------|------|------|------|
| `xaiTTSStream` | `connectTimer → failConnect()` | **No** — only rejects promise | ✅ Yes |
| `XaiRealtimeVoiceBridge` | `connectTimeout → ws.terminate()` | Yes — terminate() destroys socket | ❌ No (reverted) |

target.title: fix(codex): preserve paragraph boundaries in Codex runtime reply delivery (#109032)
target.body:
Closes #109032

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp installations using automatic visible replies with the Codex agent runtime would have multiple reply paragraphs collapsed into a single WhatsApp bubble, losing the intended conversational structure. The same configuration with the OpenClaw agent runtime correctly preserves separate bubbles.

The user-facing symptom is that the LLM's response structure (e.g., a bullet list or two distinct paragraphs) is lost when using the Codex runtime, even with `chunkMode: "newline"` and permissive block coalescing configured. The configured coalescing controls cannot recover paragraph boundaries after an earlier merge in the pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex app-server produces a single `message_start`/`message_end` cycle per turn, accumulating all paragraphs into one assistant text entry with a shared `assistantMessageIndex`. The reply pipeline's cross-index flush mechanism (`block-reply-pipeline.ts:270-276`) relies on index changes to separate logical blocks, so Codex's single index causes all paragraphs to flow into the coalescer as one payload. OpenClaw runtime avoids this by producing multiple message cycles with distinct indexes.

The fix modifies only the Codex projection boundary (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-assistant.ts`): `collectAssistantTexts()` now splits accumulated final text at paragraph boundaries using a fence-safe approach — `parseFenceSpans` + `isSafeFenceBreak` protect blank lines inside Markdown fenced code blocks from being treated as paragraph breaks. This uses the same `\n[\t ]*\n+` pattern and fence-safety mechanism already established in `EmbeddedBlockChunker` and `chunkByParagraph`.

The shared reply pipeline (`payloads.ts`, `block-streaming.ts`, coalescer, chunker) is left unchanged. Paragraph splitting lives exclusively in the Codex projection boundary, matching the codebase's architecture where the `EmbeddedBlockChunker` owns paragraph-boundary decisions in the streaming path.

## User Impact

WhatsApp users with Codex runtime and automatic visible replies will see reply paragraphs delivered as separate bubbles, matching the behavior they already get with the OpenClaw runtime. No configuration changes are needed. Non-Codex runtimes, single-paragraph replies, fenced code blocks, and media replies are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior proof** — standalone harness (51 scenarios, all production source, zero mocks):

```

[Scenario 8]  No lastAssistant, single para:                     1 payload ✓
[Scenario 9]  Empty inputs:                                      0 payloads ✓
[Scenario 10] Whitespace-only (filtered):                        1 payload ✓

[Scenario 12] Multi-paragraph without fences:                    3 parts ✓
[Scenario 13] Consecutive blank lines:                           2 parts ✓
[Scenario 14] CodexAssistantProjection — multi-paragraph:        3 parts ✓
[Scenario 15] CodexAssistantProjection — fenced code:            3 parts, fence preserved ✓
[Scenario 16] CodexAssistantProjection — single paragraph:       1 part ✓
[Scenario 17] planOutboundTextMessageUnits — newline mode:       2 units ✓
[Scenario 18] planOutboundTextMessageUnits — length mode:        1 unit ✓
[Scenario 19] planOutboundTextMessageUnits — newline + limit:    2 units ✓
=== 51 scenarios: 51 passed, 0 failed ===
```

The harness exercises three verification layers:

|-------|----------|-----------|
| **Payload builder** | `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` — canonical regression, multi-entry, error, whitespace filtering | S1–S10 |

All imported from `src/` and `extensions/codex/` — no mocks, no ESM loaders, no monkey patches.

target.title: feat(goals): continue active session goals while idle
target.body:
Related: #102260

This is the focused current-main replacement for the deterministic goal-driver slice discussed in #102261 and #103586. It deliberately does not carry forward their unrelated question, plan, judge, wait-barrier, UI, generated, or Hermes-labelled scope.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can persist, display, budget, pause, block, resume, and complete a session goal, but an active goal still stops whenever a turn ends. Operators must send another message to keep an otherwise idle goal moving.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a default-off, deterministic gateway driver that uses the existing session goal, active-run, queued-turn, system-event, heartbeat, context, UI, and `goal_changed` paths. It reserves each bounded continuation durably before enqueueing a wake, lets user work win races, and auto-pauses at the configured ceiling.

The driver is intentionally limited to agent-scoped session keys. Current-main system-event queues cannot safely distinguish the same bare `global` key in multiple agent stores, and expanding queue identity belongs in a separate change. The durable-owner repair in #104265 is also kept separate rather than duplicated here.

## User Impact

Operators who explicitly enable `tools.experimental.goalDriver.enabled` can let an active session goal continue after a fixed idle delay without sending a synthetic user message. Existing goal controls and status UI remain the source of truth. The feature remains inert by default.

## Evidence

- RED contract: fork CI at exact test-only SHA `b5c2f60d959a3714af01be27eddd00b46aa6e7e6` reported the expected missing driver, service, goal reservation/rollback, and gateway-wiring symbols: https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/actions/runs/29228761335

target.title: fix(e2e): keep text file tails UTF-8 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where E2E diagnostics that keep only the last N bytes of a text string or log file could show replacement characters when the retained byte window started in the middle of a UTF-8 character.

Related independent bug-family PRs: this PR and #109670 both keep byte-bounded diagnostic tails UTF-8 safe. They touch separate script helpers and are not stacked; either can merge first.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text-file helper now decodes truncated byte tails by dropping only leading UTF-8 continuation bytes before decoding, so byte caps stay unchanged while diagnostics remain readable. The change stays local to the E2E text-file utility and its focused tests.

## User Impact

Developers reading failed E2E diagnostics get clean tail text instead of a leading replacement character when multibyte text appears at a byte cutoff.

## Evidence

target.title: feat: add Pioneer.ai as an inference provider with live model discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw had no support for Pioneer.ai as an inference provider. Users with Pioneer.ai accounts could not use it as a model source, and there was no way to browse or select Pioneer models from the UI model picker.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds Pioneer.ai as a first-class OpenClaw inference provider with live model discovery:

- **Pioneer plugin** (`extensions/pioneer/`) registers Pioneer.ai as an OpenAI-compatible provider at `https://api.pioneer.ai/v1`. Authentication uses a `PIONEER_API_KEY` env var or auth profile.
- **Live model discovery via `augmentModelCatalog`** — The `augmentModelCatalog` hook calls the Pioneer `/v1/models` endpoint (returns `{ data: [...] }` — standard OpenAI-compatible shape parsed by the shared `getCachedLiveProviderModelRows` helper) when a Pioneer API key is configured. This is the hook that the gateway's `loadModelCatalog` → `augmentModelCatalogWithProviderPlugins` path calls, which is what feeds the UI model picker. The `catalog.run` hook (`buildPioneerCatalogResult`) is used by the CLI `models list --provider pioneer` path.
- **60-second TTL model cache** — `getCachedLiveProviderModelRows` caches live model rows for 60 seconds per provider. New models appear within one cache TTL without a gateway restart.
- **Gateway catalog warm** — A startup sidecar pre-warms the gateway model catalog on startup (read-only then full-discovery, no recurring loop) so the full Pioneer model list is available in the UI picker from the first open.
- **Provider wildcard allowlist** — Onboarding sets `pioneer/*` in `agents.defaults.models` so all live-discovered Pioneer models are visible in the picker without enumerating them individually.
- **Default model** — `pioneer/auto` is set as the default primary at onboard time, routing each request to the best available Pioneer model automatically.
- **`normalizeResolvedModel` hook** — Rewrites bare `auto` → `pioneer/auto` at transport time so the Pioneer API receives the correct routing alias.

## User Impact

- Users can now add Pioneer.ai as an inference provider and use any of its 78+ models.
- The UI model picker shows the full live Pioneer model list after gateway startup.
- New Pioneer models appear automatically within the 60s model cache TTL — no gateway restart needed.
- `pioneer/auto` as the default model means users get the best Pioneer model without manually selecting one.

## Evidence

**Live API contract** — Pioneer `/v1/models` returns `{ data: [...], first_id, last_id, has_more, object, models }` with standard OpenAI list pagination. The `data` key contains model rows with `id`, `display_name`, `max_input_tokens`, `max_tokens`, `capabilities`, etc. The shared `getCachedLiveProviderModelRows` helper parses `data` arrays by default, so no custom `readRows` override is needed.

**`pnpm openclaw models list --provider pioneer`** (auth key redacted):
```

```

target.title: fix(models): reject oversized piped auth input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readPipedStdin()` helper now enforces a 1 MiB cap (matching the existing `MATRIX_CLI_RECOVERY_KEY_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` and `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` limits). The rejection happens at the stream boundary — during the read loop, not after buffering — so oversized input never reaches auth processing.

The change follows the same buffer-chunk pattern used in the Matrix recovery-key stdin fix (PR #108120): collect `Buffer` chunks, track `totalBytes` per chunk, and throw before the cap is exceeded. Normal TTY and small piped input paths are unchanged.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `readPipedStdin`, `models auth stdin`, `paste-token unbounded` — no same-file or same-problem open PR found.

## User Impact

Piped auth commands now fail with an explicit size error for oversized input instead of buffering unbounded data. Normal interactive entry and direct arguments are unaffected.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12be34c454b75916fcf481916dec7998105820df`

### Format / diff check

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/commands/models/auth.ts src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# exit 0
```

### Real CLI proof (local, Node 24.18.0, `pnpm dev`)

Normal small piped API key reaches auth validation:

```
$ printf 'sk-test123456789\n' | OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
...
Updated config: /tmp/openclaw-test-proof/openclaw.json
Auth profile: openai:manual (openai/api_key)
```

Oversized piped input (1 MiB + 1 byte) rejected at the stdin boundary:

```
$ node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(1048577))' |     OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
Error: Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.
```

### Standalone proof (loopback stream, calls real production function)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-models-auth-stdin-limit.mts

  ok: small piped input does not trigger size rejection
  info: small_error=Failed to update auth profile store; ...
  ok: oversized piped input is rejected
  ok: rejection message is "Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes."
  info: oversized_error=Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

New test "rejects oversized piped auth input before buffering it" verifies the exact error message and confirms no downstream auth mutation.

### Mutation check

Reverted the fix to bare `input += String(chunk)` loop with no cap:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/commands/models/auth.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 39 passed (40)
```

Oversized input passes through to validate() which reports "That does not look like an OpenAI API key." instead of the size rejection. Restored fix → 40/40 pass.

### Not tested

- Full `pnpm build` with dist-based CLI (Node 22.22.0 does not meet the >=22.22.3 requirement)
- The `paste-token` oversized path (shares the same `readPipedStdin` helper as the tested `paste-api-key` path)

target.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

## Summary

- Complete the existing Control UI MCP App host bridge with safe, text-only `ui/message` support routed through the normal visible chat-send path.
- Advertise messaging only for fresh, authorized app views; reconstructed views remain explicitly read-only.
- Propagate live theme and iframe dimensions through the official MCP Apps host-context bridge without remounting, with observer/listener cleanup on teardown.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI could render MCP App resources and service app tool/resource requests, but an app could not safely ask the user to send plain text through the host chat, and mounted apps did not receive live theme or size changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the already-present iframe/resource reconstruction architecture. It reuses the existing widget-prompt validation and `WIDGET_PROMPT_EVENT` send seam, adds host-owned exact-text confirmation for MCP App requests, and uses the official `AppBridge.setHostContext` lifecycle. It does not add a second send route, config/env surface, protocol version, or privileged approval path.

The implementation adds a small explicit `readOnly` lease marker because a fresh app may legitimately have zero app-callable tools, while a transcript-reconstructed preview must remain resource-only. Tool-count inference could not represent both states safely.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, a visible and focused fresh app can request that the user send one plain-text message. The host shows the exact text for confirmation, then sends through the existing chat composer path. Hidden/background frames, empty or oversized text, slash commands, and rate-limit excesses are rejected. Apps also receive current theme and dimensions as they change.

## Independent landing and backward safety

- The gateway response field is additive. Older Control UIs ignore it; a newer UI talking to an older gateway sees the field absent and installs/advertises no message handler.
- Existing widget prompts use the same extracted validation/send helper without the MCP App confirmation callback; their existing behavior is covered by the widget-prompt and tool-card regression suites.
- App tool/resource handlers, app-only policy, sandbox origins, inner opaque iframe isolation, routes, config, and protocol versions are unchanged.
- Fresh views with an explicit authority set may advertise messaging even when that set is empty. Legacy views without authority and reconstructed `readOnly` views fail closed.
- No behavior enabled by this PR requires a later MCP Apps PR.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: all behavior remains behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Within that gate, `message.text` is advertised only when a fresh view has explicit current-run authority and the host handler is installed. Reconstructed views can still render/read resources but cannot message or call tools. Rich or multi-block `ui/message` content is intentionally unsupported.

## Evidence

- Genuine browser flow: a browser-bundled `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` ran through the real Control UI Vite app, dedicated sandbox HTTP server, and nested iframe bridge. The official initialize handshake advertised `message.text`; exact host consent was required; accepted text produced the normal `chat.send` request (`deliver: false`); the app received its response; live light-theme and container-dimension changes propagated without remounting.
- Focused exact-patch Testbox proof: 71/71 assertions passed across MCP view leases, transcript reconstruction, gateway authorization, text/focus/visibility/size/rate/slash boundaries, existing widget prompts, host-context updates, and cleanup.
- Production build passed, including the Control UI lazy chunk (`mcp-app-view-registration`, 63.20 kB) and Control UI performance limits.
- Changed-surface checks passed through formatting, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and related policy gates. An earlier Plugin SDK baseline mismatch was independently reproduced on untouched canonical main; the current canonical base includes its unrelated generated/declaration repairs.
- A first CI run exposed a production lint suppression for the SDK's request-style `onmessage` setter. The handler now registers through the SDK's exported `McpUiMessageRequestSchema`; the component and suppression-ratchet tests pass, followed by two clean fresh autoreviews.
- Two fresh full-branch autoreviews after the final safety fixes reported no actionable findings. Later canonical-base rebases were patch-identical by `git range-diff`; the last review was clean at confidence 0.88.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.widget-prompts.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:changed -- src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.ts src/gateway/mcp-app-reconstruction.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-security.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.ts ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.ts` (all relevant checks green; unrelated main-only SDK baseline mismatch noted above)
- `pnpm build`
- Fresh `$autoreview` passes before and after simplification/final safety edits

## Simplification and scope

The PR changes five production files and four focused test files. Net production growth is +68 LOC: the new schema-registered handler/host-context lifecycle and explicit read-only authority marker are offset by deleting the duplicated widget-prompt policy/send implementation. No additional abstraction module, route, config, or compatibility shim was added.

## Known gaps

- This does not enable MCP Apps globally or implement later rollout work.
- Only one plain text content block is accepted; rich content remains rejected.
- Transcript-reconstructed previews intentionally remain read-only until a fresh run grants current authority.

target.title: fix: keep channel auto-restart after abort race during backoff
target.body:
Closes #109659

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators would lose a channel permanently after a normal provider close when auto-restart backoff raced the dying run's abort signal. Gateway and container health checks stayed green while the channel never came back until a manual process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auto-restart now owns its own backoff abort lifecycle instead of sharing the dying run's `AbortSignal`. Intentional stops cancel that restart-owned supervisor, and abnormal exits clear `restartPending` with a diagnostic instead of an empty catch. No config, protocol, or public API changes.

## User Impact

When a channel connection drops, automatic restart remains reliable even if the previous run abort fires during backoff. Operators no longer need a manual gateway/container restart solely because the restart chain was swallowed silently. Intentional stops still cancel pending restarts.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox not used). Head after merge with current main: `1fae8667e`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 51 passed (exact post-merge head)

# Live gateway proof (PR head build, isolated state dir, real Telegram bot token from local config)
# Gateway: node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 19711 --bind loopback
# Provider close simulated via temporary unauthorized bot token (Telegram getMe 401),
# then manager-level auto-restart with restart-owned backoff continued the chain.
```

New/updated regression coverage:
- restart backoff sleep signal is not the dying run abort
- manual stop during backoff clears `restartPending`
- startAccount failure does not permanently kill the restart chain
- stop during restart-owned backoff clears pending without a second start

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: channel auto-restart no longer dies silently when abort races the restart backoff sleep; `restartPending` is reconciled and failures are logged; restart-owned backoff continues after a real provider close
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw PR head `1fae8667e` (merged onto current main), isolated gateway on loopback port 19711 with real Telegram channel (`@openclawwuqxuanbot`), token auth, no secrets in logs
- Current-main contrast: on main, `restart.next(abort.signal)` binds backoff to the dying run abort and `catch {}` swallows rejections, so a stop/abort during backoff can leave `restartPending: true` with no further `startChannelInternal` and no log. After this patch, backoff uses `restart.next()` (restart-owned signal only), `stopChannel` calls `restarts.get(rKey)?.cancel()`, and the catch path clears pending / logs failures
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `git merge origin/main` onto the PR branch; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` → **51 passed**
  2. Build+start gateway from this head with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / config enabling Telegram only
  3. Observe Telegram provider start (`starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)`, polling ingress started)
  4. Apply a temporary unauthorized bot token via `config.apply` to force a real Telegram provider close (`getMe` 401 / `channel exited`)
  5. Observe manager-level auto-restart with restart-owned backoff (`auto-restart attempt N/10 in Xs`) continuing across attempts instead of a silent permanent stop
  6. `channels.stop` during healthy run returns `stopped: true` with `restartPending: false` (intentional stop)
  7. Restore valid bot token; Telegram starts again (`starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)`)
- Evidence after fix (redacted gateway stdout excerpt):

```text
[gateway] http server listening (... telegram; ...)
[telegram] [default] starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started spool=.../telegram/ingress-spool-default
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.telegram.botToken, ...)
[gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[telegram] [default] channel exited: Telegram bot token unauthorized <redacted>
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[telegram] [default] channel exited: Telegram bot token unauthorized <redacted>
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 2/10 in 11s
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 3/10 in 22s
# after restoring a valid token via config.apply:
[gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
[telegram] [default] starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started spool=.../telegram/ingress-spool-default
# intentional stop while channel was running:
channels.stop telegram → {"channel":"telegram","accountId":"default","stopped":true}
channels.status → running=false, restartPending=false
```

- Control check: focused suite still **51 passed** on the exact post-merge head; live Telegram reconnect after token restore shows the restart chain is not permanently dead after provider close
- Observed result after fix: after a real Telegram provider close, the manager schedules restart-owned backoff (`auto-restart attempt … in …s`) and continues the chain; intentional `channels.stop` cancels supervision without leaving a healthy account permanently unavailable; restoring credentials allows `starting provider` again
- What was not tested: multi-hour Zalo/`zalouser` production outage, Docker healthcheck path, Discord websocket (Discord API connectivity failed on this host: ECONNREFUSED / READY timeout), other channel providers beyond Telegram + the shared manager harness

target.title: refactor(meeting-bot): extract browser meeting-bot core behind MeetingPlatformAdapter
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/google-meet` (~15k production LOC) was ~60% generic "join a WebRTC meeting site as a Chrome bot" machinery — session lifecycle, browser-tab control, virtual-audio bridging, node relay, realtime engines, setup checks, dial-in delegation — all locked inside one plugin. Adding Microsoft Teams (next PR in this track) would have meant duplicating all of it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Phase 5 of the voice-stack consolidation (follows #109413, #109466, #109497, #109640). The platform-agnostic runtime moves to core `src/meeting-bot/**` behind a new `openclaw/plugin-sdk/meeting-runtime` barrel (same pattern as `src/talk` → `realtime-voice`): session runtime with per-meeting join locks and transcript retention, browser controller (tab lifecycle, polling, recovery), node-host audio bridge (SoX, bounded queue) with injected command names, realtime agent/bidi engines, audio transports, setup-check aggregation, `voicecall.*` dial-in delegation, and the `MeetingPlatformAdapter` contract (platform owns URL semantics, in-page DOM scripts, manual-action classification, create/dial-in flows; core owns mechanism).

google-meet becomes the first adapter. Frozen ownership stays in the plugin: config keys, `googlemeet.*` gateway methods, `googlemeet` CLI, `google_meet` tool, `googlemeet.chrome` node command, health field names, `[google-meet]` log scope, Meet URL/`authuser`/locale handling, DOM selectors and scripts, Meet REST/Calendar/Drive/OAuth, Twilio dial-plan mapping.

Wire compatibility: `GoogleMeetSession`/`GoogleMeetChromeHealth` keep their exact JSON shapes (generic types aliased/intersected; the manual-action category model stays internal while adapters supply today's reason/message strings), proven by the existing exact-value test suite (274 tests green).

Three review-hardening cycles ran on the extraction (Codex gpt-5.6-sol xhigh, chunked): 13 accepted findings fixed — including per-meeting locking for dial-in joins, incompatible shared-tab reconciliation, partial-join rollback (stop transports, release tabs), one unified failed-init cleanup path for the STT engine, rejection-handled async cleanup (no unhandled rejections from fire-and-forget stops), turn/output lifecycle completion on TTS failure, manual-action propagation in browser recovery, node pull-waiter cleanup, initial-transcript trimming, and excluding Meet's `/new` creation route from reusable meeting identity. Two findings rejected as shipped-behavior contracts (echo-check ordering — documented inline; `micMuted !== true` readiness semantics).

## User Impact
