target.title: fix(plugins): cleanup session scheduler jobs on failed registration rollback (#106825)
target.body:
Closes #106825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a plugin that registers a session scheduler job and then throws during its `register` function would have its cleanup callback never invoked at the rollback boundary. The live session-scheduler record remained in module-global runtime state while the registry metadata was correctly restored — leaving external plugin-owned scheduler work (via `cleanup`) uncancelled after a failed registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registration rollback (`createPluginRegistrationTransaction`) restores the registry snapshot and calls `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` to clean up commands, interactive handlers, code-mode namespaces, context engines, and hooks — but did not clean up session scheduler jobs. These jobs are stored in two layers: a `registry.sessionSchedulerJobs` array (cleaned by the snapshot restore) and a separate module-global Map in `host-hook-runtime.ts` (previously never cleaned on rollback).

The fix adds the existing `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs` call to the `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` function in `registry.ts`, filtered to the rolling-back plugin's records. The cleanup is fire-and-forget (`void`) because the rollback lifecycle is synchronous while the cleanup callbacks may be async (external resource cancellation). Any cleanup failures are logged as warnings via `pushDiagnostic`.

## User Impact

Plugins that register session scheduler jobs with a `cleanup` callback will now have that callback invoked when their registration transaction is rolled back (e.g., a later exception during the same `register` function). No functional change for the common case where registration succeeds or where no session scheduler job is registered.

## Evidence

**Focused regression test** — `plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts` (3 tests, all passing):

```
 ✓ plugins src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts (3 tests) 82ms
```

**Real-behavior proof script** (standalone `tsx` harness exercising production code paths — `createPluginRegistry` → `createPluginRegistrationTransaction` → `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` → `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs`):

Before rollback: 1 live job, 1 registry entry
After rollback:
- cleanup callback calls: 1
- cleanup context: {"reason":"disable","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","jobId":"audit-job"}
- live jobs: [] (removed from module-global state)
- registry sessionSchedulerJobs: [] (restored by snapshot)

All three assertions pass: cleanup invoked once, live record removed, registry snapshot restored.

**Existing contract tests** — `scheduled-turns.contract.test.ts` (24 tests) and `run-context-lifecycle.contract.test.ts` (15 tests) both pass unaffected.

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using opencode with review by the author.

target.title: Prevent repeated byte-triggered compactions
target.body:
## Summary

- prevent repeated byte-triggered preflight compactions for the same active transcript when a previous byte-triggered compaction did not materially reduce the transcript below the configured threshold
- record byte-triggered compaction retry state on `SessionEntry` so retries require the same threshold, the same active session file, and material new growth
- preserve token-triggered preflight compaction behavior, including token compaction taking precedence when the byte retry is suppressed

## What Problem This Solves

When `agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured, a byte-triggered preflight compaction can legitimately leave the active successor transcript above the threshold (for example when transcript rotation preserves branch/state history). Without retry hysteresis, the next turn can immediately trigger another byte-based preflight compaction, producing a repeated compaction loop.

This patch records the post-compaction active transcript size/file/threshold for byte-triggered compactions and suppresses another byte-triggered retry for that same active transcript until it grows materially. A retry is allowed when the active file changes, the threshold changes, or the transcript grows by at least `max(1 MiB, 10%)` from the previously recorded byte size.

Token-triggered compaction remains unchanged.

## Related

Adjacent to #88188 because both involve `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` behavior, but this PR handles the opposite failure mode: byte-triggered preflight compaction firing repeatedly after a prior byte-triggered compaction leaves the active transcript above threshold.

## Real setup tested

Staged runtime validation in a clean upstream checkout on the current branch. The proof harness used a temporary session store/transcript file, called the real `runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` runtime path, and replaced only the compaction executor with a recording stub so the trigger/skip decision still came from the production preflight guard. No production runtime or private deployment state was used for PR validation.

## Exact steps or command run after this patch

From the repository checkout:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.ts \
  src/config/sessions/types.ts \
  src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts

git diff --check

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
  -p tsconfig.core.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-byteguard.tsbuildinfo
```

## Evidence

- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`: 53 tests passed
- `session-updates.test.ts` + `session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts`: 5 tests passed
- `tsgo` core project check passed
- formatting check passed
- diff whitespace check passed

New coverage includes:

- first byte-threshold crossing still triggers preflight compaction
- same active transcript + same threshold + no material growth suppresses repeated byte-triggered compaction
- changed active session file does not suppress retry
- changed threshold does not suppress retry
- material transcript growth allows retry
- token-triggered compaction still runs when byte retry is suppressed
- rotated successor file and byte size are recorded after byte-triggered compaction
- byte-triggered metadata is persisted through `incrementCompactionCount`
- ordinary token compactions do not write byte-triggered retry metadata

## Observed result after fix

The repeated byte-trigger retry condition is blocked for the same active transcript until there is material new growth, while token-triggered compaction and legitimate byte retries remain available.

Additional staged runtime proof from `tmp/pr-95885-proof/run-preflight-compaction-proof.ts` on head `bba688c7bc9de4aa9d511591a4b1a77b7ddacb34`:

```json
{"step":"byte-trigger first preflight","compactCallsBefore":0,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"transcript_bytes","currentTokenCount":124,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"byte-trigger same transcript retry","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":false,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"token-trigger still compacts","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":2,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"tokens","currentTokenCount":902,"sessionId":"token-session","compactionCount":1}
{"proof":"summary","totalCompactCalls":2,"triggers":["transcript_bytes","tokens"]}
```

This covers the runtime behavior ClawSweeper requested: the first byte-threshold crossing still compacts, the same active transcript/threshold retry is suppressed when there is no material growth, and token-triggered compaction still runs.


## What was not tested

- No production runtime or private deployment state was used.
- This PR does not change successor transcript pruning semantics; it only prevents immediate retry loops when a byte-triggered compaction does not materially shrink the active transcript.
- End-to-end UI notification behavior is not changed or tested here.

target.title: feat(teams): add exact-tab workspace sharing
target.body:
Refs #105322.

Builds on the Workspaces foundation landed in #104139.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's operator dashboard is intentionally single-operator and privileged. Teams need a narrower way to share selected workspace tabs with external members without exposing chat, gateway state, global presence, other workspaces, or workspace administration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- add opt-in, gateway-local Teams accounts, opaque sessions, one-time invites, and a scope-less `member` role
- add exact resource RBAC, domain isolation, server-attested agent delegation, and host-bound plugin Teams primitives
- partition Workspaces by isolation domain and support exact-tab read, request-change, and write access
- add a restricted `/teams` portal with owner invite/review controls and no operator dashboard navigation or global gateway state

### Security and privacy boundaries

- member sockets receive no gateway-global presence, health, defaults, chat, or plugin broadcasts
- remote plaintext Teams authentication is rejected; loopback HTTP remains an explicit local-development path
- invite codes and session tokens are omitted from ordinary JSON/list responses and browser persistence
- invited users and delegated agents cannot receive workspace-admin or sharing-admin authority in v1
- CLI-backed agent harnesses carry the server-owned Teams subject only through an opaque loopback grant; the subject is cache-bound and is not projected into child environment variables, headers, or plugin-visible context fields
- logout, expiry, revocation, membership removal, and grant removal are revalidated against open member sessions

## User Impact

- Workspace owners can invite a member and grant exact-tab `read`, `request changes`, or `write` access.
- Members use a restricted `/teams` portal rather than the privileged operator Control UI.
- Requests for changes return to the owning user for approval; members and agents cannot become workspace or sharing administrators in v1.
- The feature remains local and opt-in. It adds no SaaS identity, email delivery, SSO/SCIM, billing, cross-gateway federation, telemetry, or member access to the normal operator dashboard.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto upstream main at `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`; all 21 commits are preserved in order and patch-equivalent to the reviewed `a03df5fd` stack. The earlier conflict adaptations retain current main's inline Gateway client metadata and mobile-bootstrap pairing guard while layering Teams role/scopes/capabilities and member-pairing eligibility into those current contracts.
- Final-head focused proof passed 285 uniquely routed tests: plugin contracts 12, suspension admission 8, Gateway client plus Teams portal 68, pairing 32, optional tools 85, delegation authorization 49, Teams API 14, and Workspaces schema 17.
- Plugin SDK API-baseline verification and the complete SDK surface check passed; docs-map generation, dead-code unused-file validation, type-aware UI lint, scoped lint/formatting, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- The earlier broader changed-gateway run passed 2,014 of 2,017 assertions; the only failures were three project copies of the same unchanged upstream MCP shutdown-timing test. GitHub Actions remains the canonical broad and install-aligned type gate.
- Bootstrap -> invite -> exact read -> cross-tab denial -> session revocation integration coverage is included in the green focused suites.

target.title: Guard Skill Workshop update applies against delta drafts
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes a Skill Workshop update-apply footgun where an update proposal that contains a delta/proposal note can be applied as the full replacement `SKILL.md`.

For update proposals, `applySkillProposal()` strips proposal frontmatter and writes the proposal body as the live skill content. That is correct when the proposal body is a full updated skill, but unsafe when the body is an update note such as `# Update Proposal ...` with "proposed changes" instructions. In that case apply can replace the existing skill workflow with a proposal stub.

This PR adds an apply-time guard for update proposals before the live write, while still allowing intentional complete rewrites of a skill body.

## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop `action=update` proposals are meant to carry a complete replacement `SKILL.md`. Before this guard, apply-time code could accept a proposal/delta note and write that note as the live skill body. That risks destroying the actual skill procedure.

The guard should reject obvious non-skill update notes and identity swaps, but it should not block valid complete rewrites just because the new skill reorganizes or consolidates sections. This matters for legitimate skill maintenance where a full replacement may intentionally change the old section layout.

## What changed

- Reject update proposal bodies that have no replacement skill body / no top-level skill heading.
- Reject update proposal bodies that look like delta/proposal notes instead of complete skill bodies, using multiple proposal-note markers instead of a single broad substring match.
- Reject update proposal bodies that change the existing skill identity heading.
- Allow complete replacement `SKILL.md` bodies that intentionally reorganize or consolidate old `##` sections.
- Preserve compatibility for existing valid skills that have frontmatter plus prose but no top-level H1 heading.
- Add regression coverage for:
  - delta/proposal-note update drafts;
  - empty replacement bodies;
  - complete section rewrites;
  - single proposal-like section headings inside an otherwise complete skill;
  - emoji-decorated preserved headings.

## Duplicate/adjacent work check

I checked current `origin/main` and searched open/closed issues and PRs before opening this PR.

Not duplicates:

- #92733 touches `applySkillProposal()` for openclaw-managed skill roots, but it still writes `stripProposalFrontmatterForSkill(content)` directly and does not validate that update content is a complete skill body.
- #94315 / #94249 cover large-proposal apply timeout behavior.
- #90421 / #90388 cover stale proposal reconciliation when a target skill already exists or disappears.
- #95395 / #94947 cover `action=create` proposals that should have targeted existing skills.

This PR is specifically about update-apply content-shape validation before overwriting an existing `SKILL.md`.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel non-OK streaming card response body before throwing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`FeishuStreamingSession` makes HTTP requests to the Feishu/Lark API through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. When the API returns a non-OK response, the code throws immediately without canceling the response body in three paths:

1. `assertSuccessfulCardKitResponse` — card update/replace/note/close requests
2. `getToken` — tenant access token fetch
3. `start()` — card creation request

The `release()` call in `finally` blocks does not consume or cancel the upstream response stream, so the unconsumed body keeps connections open until garbage collection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the same pattern as our merged PRs #109519 (Google Chat), #109508 (docs), #109525 (ClawRouter), and #109701 (MS Teams file consent) — cancel the response body before throwing on non-OK paths.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. Prevents resource leaks from unconsumed response bodies when Feishu API requests fail with non-OK status codes (e.g. rate limiting, auth failures, service unavailable).

## Evidence

Two new tests:
- **cancels a non-OK tenant-token response body before throwing** — mocks `/auth/` to return 503, verifies `body.cancel()` was called once before the throw propagates
- **cancels a non-OK card-create response body before throwing** — mocks card creation to return 503, verifies `body.cancel()` was called once

target.title: fix(sandbox): cancel unsuccessful CDP probe responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sandbox browser startup could leave HTTP response streams open when CDP readiness probes received non-success statuses. Each failed `/json/version` probe during the retry loop could retain transport resources until garbage collection while startup still timed out normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForSandboxCdp` now cancels unread response bodies after non-ok probe responses. Successful probes, retry timing, auth headers, and startup timeout behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox browser auto-start still fails the same way when CDP never becomes ready, but failed probe responses release their connections promptly instead of being left open across retries.

## Evidence

**Real-machine before / premise / after / negative control**

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.5.0.

I ran the same production-function harness from an `upstream/main` snapshot and this branch. The harness starts a real localhost `node:http` server, sends a streaming HTTP 503 response through real Node fetch, calls the production `waitForSandboxCdp` loop, and observes the server-side TCP socket 250 ms after the function returns:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-before
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /srv/projects/openclaw-wt-sandbox-cdp-body-cancel
```

The harness loads the probe loop from `src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts` (mirrored in `/tmp/sandbox-cdp-probe-*.ts` for import isolation). The server never ends its response body, making socket closure a direct observation of consumer cancellation rather than normal body completion.

Negative control / before (`upstream/main` at `e01027dd28a`):

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":false}
```

Premise: non-ok CDP probes returned immediately without consuming or canceling unread error bodies, so the streaming response stayed open after the probe loop moved on.

After (`3b933448b77`):

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
```

The identical `cdpReachable: false` value is the behavioral control: startup semantics are preserved while the real server observes prompt connection release.

Focused validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts -t "cancels the CDP probe response body"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 47 skipped (48)

./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
exit 0
```

Full build and broader suites were not run locally; fork GitHub Actions are expected to cover wider gates. This is a non-visual transport cleanup, so no screenshot is applicable.

AI-assisted: Yes. Cursor agent reviewed the sandbox CDP probe loop, sibling body-cancel fixes, tests, and real-machine evidence.

target.title: fix(coding-agent): isolate Codex CLI CODEX_HOME from OpenClaw OAuth in skill launch forms
target.body:
Closes #109704

AI-assisted: built with Codex

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the bundled `coding-agent` skill's documented Codex CLI
launch forms use the ambient `CODEX_HOME` (`~/.codex` default), which can share
the same ChatGPT OAuth credential with OpenClaw's own `openai` provider.
When both clients use the same account's refresh token, one client can consume
or rotate the token, causing the other to fail with `refresh_token_reused`.
This leaves OpenClaw unable to make model requests until manual re-authentication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `coding-agent` skill's documented `codex exec` launch forms now scope
Codex CLI to a dedicated `CODEX_HOME` kept **outside** every Git worktree so it
never discovers the ambient `~/.codex` credential and never places OAuth
credentials (`auth.json`) inside a checkout the coding worker may commit from.

Three locations are updated:

- **Hard rule**: instructs operators to create a `CODEX_HOME` outside every Git
  worktree (`mkdir -p <safe-path> && chmod 700 <safe-path>`), authenticate once,
  and prepend it to every `codex exec` launch. Warns that `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`
  must never be staged or committed.
- **Codex launch form**: uses `/safe/path/.codex-isolated` instead of a
  worktree-relative path.
- **Scratch Codex**: allocates a dedicated `mktemp -d` directory outside
  `$SCRATCH` with mode 700 instead of creating `.codex-home` inside the scratch
  repo.

The runtime's bounded-turn path already isolates `CODEX_HOME`; this fix brings
the skill's manual launch forms into alignment with a safe external-home
convention.

## User Impact

Users who authenticate both OpenClaw and Codex CLI with the same ChatGPT
account no longer risk OpenClaw OAuth breakage when the `coding-agent` skill
launches a Codex worker. Codex credentials and session state are never placed
inside a Git checkout.

## Evidence

Runtime already isolates CODEX_HOME in the bounded-turn path:

```
extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts:101  codexHome = path.join(workspace.dir, "codex-home")
extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts:282  CODEX_HOME: codexHome
```

Skill launch forms before this change (ambient `~/.codex`):

```
bash ... command:"codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Skill launch forms after this change (scoped, external, mode 700):

```
bash ... command:"CODEX_HOME=/safe/path/.codex-isolated codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Scratch Codex before (CODEX_HOME inside git repo):

```
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/.codex-home"
... command:"codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Scratch Codex after (CODEX_HOME outside git repo, mode 700):

```
CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 700 "$CODEX_HOME"
... command:"CODEX_HOME=$CODEX_HOME codex exec - < \"$PROMPT\""
```

Docs-only change; no runtime behavior, tests, or build output affected.

target.title: fix(feishu): lock timeoutMs preflight abort for stalled DNS lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app registration goes through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. Operators need a locked regression that a **stalled DNS/proxy preflight** is cancelled by the guard's existing top-level `timeoutMs` before any HTTP request is dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1 on the prior tip identified that the `signal: AbortSignal.timeout()` path in `fetchFeishuJson` drops guard-owned timeout diagnostics. This iteration restores `timeoutMs` (the guard's top-level param), keeping the shared `request timed out` diagnostic and `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` preflight abort.

**This iteration:**
- Rebased on latest `main`
- **Kept** guard `timeoutMs` (no production ownership change)
- Added stalled-lookup regression next to the existing hang-POST timeout proof, matching its outcome shape
- No production code changed — test-only addition (+27 lines)

## User Impact

- **Before:** No focused Feishu registration test that a never-resolving lookup aborts under `timeoutMs` without HTTP dispatch.
- **After:** That contract is locked; registration timeout semantics stay on the shared guard owner.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `d60a33276f8`
**Base:** `92e5a10f1a9`

### Regression test suite (11/11 pass)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts --reporter verbose extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ Feishu app registration > defaults unsafe begin polling lifetimes 241ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > clamps unsafe poll sleeps 19ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > prints scan-to-create QR codes 2ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > times out registration POSTs (TCP hang) 95ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > rejects with timeout when preflight lookup stalls 83ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > rejects Feishu API responses that exceed 16 MiB cap 232ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > parses under-cap JSON 50ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > sends bound reads through real SSRF guard 11ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > wraps malformed JSON with feishu.api error 8ms
 ✓ feishu bound reads > rejects oversized response (OOM guard) 114ms
 ✓ feishu bound reads > parses well-formed JSON under cap 31ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
 Start at  16:36:03
 Duration  7.17s
```

### Matched outcome shape

| Assertion | Existing POST hang test | New stalled-DNS test |
|---|---|---|
| abort mechanism | `timeoutMs` → guard `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` | `timeoutMs` → guard `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` |
| outcome | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` | `TimeoutError` |
| `fetch_called` | reaches TCP listener | false |
| elapsed | 88ms | 82ms |

### Stalled-lookup proof output

```
✓ |extension-feishu| Feishu app registration > rejects with timeout when preflight lookup stalls (DNS/proxy stall protection) 83ms
  [feishu preflight stall proof] timed_out name=TimeoutError elapsed_ms=82 fetch_called=0
```

- `elapsed_ms=82` — guard timeout fired within the 80ms window
- `fetch_called=0` — no HTTP request was dispatched (aborted during DNS preflight)

### Test code

Located at `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts:379-404` — placed as sibling of the existing "times out registration POSTs when accounts never return headers" test, using identical outcome shape (`timeoutMs: 80`, `then/catch` split, same elapsed window).

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified

target.title: [Bug]: plugin metadata conflict can block gateway startup, and plugin repair/reinstall can silently drop plugin config/allowlist causing state drift
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On macOS, upgrading an existing npm/Homebrew-style OpenClaw install to `2026.7.1` can leave external plugins in a split-brain state:

1. a legacy plugin install metadata conflict prevents startup migrations from completing, so the gateway refuses readiness
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` does **not** clear it
3. after manual uninstall/reinstall of the conflicting plugin, the gateway can recover, but other external plugins may still have stale install/index state
4. during follow-up repair, a working plugin can silently lose its config entry / allowlist entry / API-key subtree, so the plugin is physically installed and partially loaded, but the capability is unusable until config is manually restored
5. even after successful recovery and a real successful capability call, some status surfaces still report old version drift

This leaves the system operational only after manual intervention across multiple layers (`plugins.entries.*`, `plugins.allow`, plugin reinstall, gateway restart), and the built-in repair flow does not converge state automatically.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a long-lived macOS install with external plugins already configured.

Environment before upgrade:
- OpenClaw `2026.6.11`
- macOS arm64
- Homebrew global install under `/opt/homebrew`
- external plugins present: `openclaw-weixin`, `@openclaw/deepseek-provider`, `@openclaw/tavily-plugin`
- web search configured to use `tavily`
- Tavily API key stored under plugin config

Upgrade flow:

1. Upgrade OpenClaw core to `2026.7.1`
2. Ensure Node is compatible (`v24.18.0` in this repro)
3. Run:
   - `openclaw gateway install`
   - `openclaw gateway start`
4. Observe gateway never becomes ready
5. `openclaw gateway status --deep` shows service loaded/running or restarting, but probe fails / port not truly ready
6. Logs show:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

7. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`
8. Observe the same plugin install metadata conflict remains; gateway still not ready
9. Manually force-uninstall and reinstall the conflicting plugin:
   - `openclaw plugins uninstall openclaw-weixin --force`
   - `openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin`
   - `openclaw plugins registry --refresh`
   - `openclaw gateway restart`
10. Gateway finally becomes healthy
11. Now inspect other external plugins (`deepseek`, `tavily`): installed files are present on disk, but status/index surfaces still show old versions or disabled state
12. Attempt a real Tavily call:

```bash
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --limit 3 --query "OpenClaw 2026.7.1 release notes" --json
```

13. It fails with missing credential error, even though Tavily was previously configured:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

14. Inspect current config vs backup:
   - `tools.web.search.provider` is still `tavily`
   - but `plugins.entries.tavily` is gone
   - and `tavily` is missing from `plugins.allow`
   - backup config still contains the Tavily API key subtree
15. Manually restore the missing config and allowlist entries, restart gateway, rerun the direct search test
16. Tavily search succeeds, but some status surfaces can still report stale install/version drift

### Expected behavior

- A plugin install metadata conflict should not permanently block startup without a supported convergence path.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` should either resolve the conflict or provide a deterministic repair path.
- Manual uninstall/reinstall of one conflicting plugin should not silently remove config/allowlist/credential subtrees for other working plugins.
- If a plugin capability is actually working again, status surfaces should converge and stop reporting stale drift.
- The combined repair path should be idempotent.

### Actual behavior

- Gateway readiness is blocked by a plugin install metadata conflict.
- `doctor --fix` does not converge the state.
- Manual plugin reinstall is required to recover gateway readiness.
- Another plugin (`tavily`) can lose its config entry, allowlist membership, and API-key subtree during the repair sequence.
- After manual config restoration, the capability works again, but some status/index views still report old version drift or disabled state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

macOS arm64

### Install method

npm/Homebrew global install

### Model

MiniMax-M3 (not material to the bug)

### Provider / routing chain

- `minimax-portal` for agent runs
- `tavily` for managed web search
- `openclaw-weixin` channel configured

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway managed via macOS LaunchAgent
- external plugins involved in the repro: `openclaw-weixin`, `deepseek`, `tavily`
- Tavily was previously configured and functioning before repair

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Representative blocking log:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

Representative post-repair Tavily failure:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

Representative successful direct Tavily test only after manual config restoration:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "provider": "tavily"
}
```

State observations during recovery:
- `plugins.entries.tavily` missing from current config
- `tavily` missing from `plugins.allow`
- backup config still contained Tavily `webSearch.apiKey`
- direct capability call worked again only after restoring both config entry and allowlist
- some status surfaces still reported stale Tavily version/install drift after the capability was already working

### Impact and severity

High.

This can leave an upgraded install in a state where:
- gateway will not start
- official repair does not converge state
- user must manually inspect config/state internals
- plugin credentials/config can be silently dropped during recovery
- status surfaces remain misleading even after functional recovery

### Additional information

This seems related to, but not fully covered by, existing plugin metadata conflict/state-drift issues such as:
- #97563
- #97768
- #90418
- #107727

What seems unique here is the full chain:
- plugin metadata conflict blocks startup
- doctor cannot clear it
- manual conflicting-plugin reinstall restores gateway
- another plugin then loses config/allowlist/credentials
- capability works again only after manual config restoration
- status/index can still drift after successful functional recovery

A robust fix likely needs all of the following:
- a deterministic source of truth for external plugin install state
- safe, idempotent reconciliation between legacy install index, SQLite state, config entries, and allowlist
- repair tooling that can restore plugin config references without silently dropping unrelated plugin credentials
- status surfaces that reflect actual loaded/working capability state after recovery

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), rejects empty bodies, and gates zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy — preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Zero-overlap update proposals are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The zero-overlap approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for zero-overlap updates while ordinary updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `92683fcb1a`**

**Terminal output from exact head** (real Skill Workshop apply flow via `node --import tsx`, 5 scenarios including incidental-overlap):

```console
=== Real Behavior Proof: Skill Workshop Apply-Body Validation ===
SHA: 92683fcb1a
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T08:28:38.286Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Zero-overlap (unrelated) update requires explicit approval ---
Original SKILL.md content:
---
name: weather
description: Weather lookup skill
---

# Weather

Steps to check weather.
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: true
Apply result.changeSummary: +4 lines, -4 lines
SKILL.md after apply contains "deploying to production": true
SKILL.md changed from original: true

--- Proof 2: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
SKILL.md before rejection:
---
name: empty-test
description: Empty test target
---

# Empty Test

Original content that must survive.
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged: true

--- Proof 3: Headingless skill update succeeds without explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -2 lines
SKILL.md contains "save the result to disk": true

--- Proof 4: Valid update with shared content succeeds ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines
SKILL.md contains "Updated steps": true
Rollback.previousContent contains "Steps to check weather": true

--- Proof 5: Incidental shared-line plan does NOT require explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +8 lines, -3 lines
Note: This proposal shares "# Weather" line but is a plan document; overlap classifier sees shared line and does not flag it as requiresExplicitApproval. The canonical parseFrontmatter validation ensures it has valid frontmatter (name, description) and non-empty body, which structurally valid plan documents do have.

=== Summary ===
1. Zero-overlap update: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
2. Empty body rejection: SKILL.md unchanged ✅
3. Headingless skill update: requiresExplicitApproval=false, succeeds ✅
4. Valid update with shared content: requiresExplicitApproval=false, changeSummary + rollback ✅
5. Incidental shared-line plan: requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected, not flagged as risky) ✅

Overlap classifier behavior:
- Zero shared lines (complete rewrite/unrelated): requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
- Any shared lines (ordinary edit or incidental overlap): requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
- Structural validation (canonical parseFrontmatter) catches empty bodies and invalid frontmatter regardless of overlap
```

**Unit tests (exact head SHA 92683fcb1a)**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts --run

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts (2 tests) 2588ms
     ✓ gates zero-overlap updates with requiresExplicitApproval and rejects empty bodies  1813ms
     ✓ applies headingless and overlapping updates without requiresExplicitApproval  769ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Validation matrix**:

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental shared line (plan shares heading)    => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned, rollback recorded
```

**CI note**: The `startup-memory` check failure (`status --json` median RSS exceeding 425 MB limit) is a pre-existing issue on the `main` branch, not introduced by this PR. All other CI checks (oxlint, format, typecheck, tests, docs) passed.

target.title: fix(models): reject oversized piped auth input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readPipedStdin()` helper now enforces a 1 MiB cap (matching the existing `MATRIX_CLI_RECOVERY_KEY_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` and `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` limits). The rejection happens at the stream boundary — during the read loop, not after buffering — so oversized input never reaches auth processing.

The change follows the same buffer-chunk pattern used in the Matrix recovery-key stdin fix (PR #108120): collect `Buffer` chunks, track `totalBytes` per chunk, and throw before the cap is exceeded. Normal TTY and small piped input paths are unchanged.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `readPipedStdin`, `models auth stdin`, `paste-token unbounded` — no same-file or same-problem open PR found.

## User Impact

Piped auth commands now fail with an explicit size error for oversized input instead of buffering unbounded data. Normal interactive entry and direct arguments are unaffected.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12be34c454b75916fcf481916dec7998105820df`

### Format / diff check

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/commands/models/auth.ts src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# exit 0
```

### Real CLI proof (local, Node 24.18.0, `pnpm dev`)

Normal small piped API key reaches auth validation:

```
$ printf 'sk-test123456789\n' | OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
...
Updated config: /tmp/openclaw-test-proof/openclaw.json
Auth profile: openai:manual (openai/api_key)
```

Oversized piped input (1 MiB + 1 byte) rejected at the stdin boundary:

```
$ node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(1048577))' |     OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
Error: Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.
```

### Standalone proof (loopback stream, calls real production function)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-models-auth-stdin-limit.mts

  ok: small piped input does not trigger size rejection
  info: small_error=Failed to update auth profile store; ...
  ok: oversized piped input is rejected
  ok: rejection message is "Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes."
  info: oversized_error=Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

New test "rejects oversized piped auth input before buffering it" verifies the exact error message and confirms no downstream auth mutation.

### Mutation check

Reverted the fix to bare `input += String(chunk)` loop with no cap:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/commands/models/auth.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 39 passed (40)
```

Oversized input passes through to validate() which reports "That does not look like an OpenAI API key." instead of the size rejection. Restored fix → 40/40 pass.

### Not tested

- Full `pnpm build` with dist-based CLI (Node 22.22.0 does not meet the >=22.22.3 requirement)
- The `paste-token` oversized path (shares the same `readPipedStdin` helper as the tested `paste-api-key` path)

target.title: fix(ci): bound docs-sync publish repo git clone

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `docs-sync-publish` workflow could remain stuck in the `git clone` step until the job timeout when the Git transport to `openclaw/docs.git` stalls. This blocks the entire documentation publish pipeline and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `git clone` command now runs through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). Ref selection, shallow checkout, build, warmup, and sync behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers get a prompt, actionable checkout failure instead of losing a docs-publish runner for the full job timeout before the sync begins.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts --run --testNamePattern="bounds docs-sync publish repo git clone"` ??1 passed.

- Controlled runtime proof extracted the production workflow step, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a Git transport that stalls until `TERM`. The step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds, the Git fixture observed `TERM`, and did not reach the five-second outer watchdog. The identical pattern was proven for all five Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete test suite was also attempted: 72 tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases failed because the isolated host lacked GitHub CLI authentication/clean login-shell state. The affected focused regression is green.

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Catalog-path coverage proves Tool Search / Code Mode preserves plugin result control.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- 68 focused tests passed across agent-core, embedded-agent, adapter, catalog, session-yield, and Plugin SDK suites.
- Package tests type-check: `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.packages.json`.
- Agent tests type-check: `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents.json`.
- Plugin SDK declaration build passes: `tsconfig.plugin-sdk.dts.json`.

target.title: fix(signal): reject non-decimal status reaction ids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal status-reaction handling kept a secondary message-ID timestamp fallback that is not reachable from the current Signal receive path. The fallback made the status-reaction target look broader than the real runtime contract and could not be proven with a real Signal event.

## Why This Change Was Made

- No production code changed — test-only addition (+27 lines)

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), rejects empty bodies, and gates zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy — preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Zero-overlap update proposals are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The zero-overlap approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for zero-overlap updates while ordinary updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, **exact head SHA `92683fcb1a`**

**Terminal output from exact head** (real Skill Workshop apply flow via `node --import tsx`, 5 scenarios including incidental-overlap):

```console
=== Real Behavior Proof: Skill Workshop Apply-Body Validation ===
SHA: 92683fcb1a
Timestamp: 2026-07-17T08:28:38.286Z
Node: v24.13.1
Platform: linux

--- Proof 1: Zero-overlap (unrelated) update requires explicit approval ---
Original SKILL.md content:
---
name: weather
description: Weather lookup skill
---

# Weather

Steps to check weather.
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: true
Apply result.changeSummary: +4 lines, -4 lines
SKILL.md after apply contains "deploying to production": true
SKILL.md changed from original: true

--- Proof 2: Empty body hard rejection preserves SKILL.md ---
SKILL.md before rejection:
---
name: empty-test
description: Empty test target
---

# Empty Test

Original content that must survive.
Rejection error: Proposal body is empty after stripping proposal-only frontmatter. The proposal must contain the complete skill content.
SKILL.md unchanged: true

--- Proof 3: Headingless skill update succeeds without explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -2 lines
SKILL.md contains "save the result to disk": true

--- Proof 4: Valid update with shared content succeeds ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +3 lines, -3 lines
SKILL.md contains "Updated steps": true
Rollback.previousContent contains "Steps to check weather": true

--- Proof 5: Incidental shared-line plan does NOT require explicit approval ---
Apply result.requiresExplicitApproval: false
Apply result.changeSummary: +8 lines, -3 lines
Note: This proposal shares "# Weather" line but is a plan document; overlap classifier sees shared line and does not flag it as requiresExplicitApproval. The canonical parseFrontmatter validation ensures it has valid frontmatter (name, description) and non-empty body, which structurally valid plan documents do have.

=== Summary ===
1. Zero-overlap update: requiresExplicitApproval=true ✅
2. Empty body rejection: SKILL.md unchanged ✅
3. Headingless skill update: requiresExplicitApproval=false, succeeds ✅
4. Valid update with shared content: requiresExplicitApproval=false, changeSummary + rollback ✅
5. Incidental shared-line plan: requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected, not flagged as risky) ✅

Overlap classifier behavior:
- Zero shared lines (complete rewrite/unrelated): requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
- Any shared lines (ordinary edit or incidental overlap): requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
- Structural validation (canonical parseFrontmatter) catches empty bodies and invalid frontmatter regardless of overlap
```

**Unit tests (exact head SHA 92683fcb1a)**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts --run

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/apply-body-validation.test.ts (2 tests) 2588ms
     ✓ gates zero-overlap updates with requiresExplicitApproval and rejects empty bodies  1813ms
     ✓ applies headingless and overlapping updates without requiresExplicitApproval  769ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Validation matrix**:

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection, SKILL.md unchanged
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Incidental shared line (plan shares heading)    => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false, follows configured policy
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned, rollback recorded
```

**CI note**: The `startup-memory` check failure (`status --json` median RSS exceeding 425 MB limit) is a pre-existing issue on the `main` branch, not introduced by this PR. All other CI checks (oxlint, format, typecheck, tests, docs) passed.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): treat blank env API keys as unconfigured
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `XI_API_KEY` environment values are truthy strings, so the ElevenLabs providers treated them as real credentials:

- `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured` returned `true` when `XI_API_KEY="  "`, so auto-selection could pick the realtime provider and only fail later at connection time.
- `transcribeElevenLabsAudio` skipped its `ElevenLabs API key missing` guard and sent the speech-to-text request with an empty `xi-api-key` header, surfacing as a confusing upstream 401 instead of a clear local configuration error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-file key path already normalizes blanks (`normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`), and the profile fallback already trims (`resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`). Only the raw env fallbacks bypassed normalization. This routes them (plus the request-level key, matching the merged xAI handling in `realtime-transcription-provider.ts`) through the same shared `normalizeOptionalString` helper so blank values are treated as missing everywhere in this provider.

## Changes

- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`: `isConfigured` and `createSession` resolve the `XI_API_KEY` fallback via `normalizeOptionalString`, so whitespace-only values report unconfigured and session creation fails fast with `ElevenLabs API key missing`.
- `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`: the speech-to-text key resolution normalizes `req.apiKey`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `XI_API_KEY` with the same helper, so blank values are skipped and env keys are trimmed before being sent.
- Regression tests: whitespace-only env keys are treated as missing in both providers (including asserting no request is sent), and a padded env key is trimmed before use.

## User Impact

Operators with a whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`XI_API_KEY` (e.g., a placeholder left in an env file) now get a clear "ElevenLabs API key missing" error and the realtime provider correctly reports itself unconfigured, instead of a request sent with an empty credential that fails upstream. Real keys are unaffected (verified trimmed-to-same-value in tests). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/` — 38/38 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in changed files (only pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors from a stale local dependency install).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Real HTTP proof below: loopback server + production functions, before/after this patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A whitespace-only `XI_API_KEY` made the realtime provider report configured, and the speech-to-text path sent a real request carrying an empty `xi-api-key` header instead of failing fast locally.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production functions imported directly from the changed sources, real `node:http` loopback server as the ElevenLabs API endpoint (`request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` to permit the loopback target). Current head: `446eea15d5535b6f0c64b2dca9c6d01047f43bac`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/elk-proof/proof.mts` with `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=""` and `XI_API_KEY="  "` in the environment. The driver starts a real HTTP server, calls `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured({ providerConfig: {} })`, then calls the production `transcribeElevenLabsAudio({ buffer, fileName, mime, baseUrl: <loopback>, request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true } })` and reads the server's received-request count and captured `xi-api-key` header back.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): true`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: resolved (request was sent)`, `server received requests: 1`, `captured xi-api-key header: ""`. **What was not tested:** No live ElevenLabs API calls (no real credential available); the loopback server stands in for the upstream endpoint. The realtime websocket session path was not connected end-to-end with a blank key; its `isConfigured`/`createSession` gates are covered by the new unit tests and the same normalization helper. No UI changes.

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other providers' env credential paths (bedrock was handled in #109680, `packages/ai` env keys in #109691, deepgram in #108565); this PR is scoped to ElevenLabs only.
- The config-file `apiKey` handling, which already normalizes blanks via `normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`.
- `resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`, which already trims its env read.

target.title: fix: require decimal numeric oc-path predicates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users filtering oc-path results with numeric predicates could match non-decimal values when the predicate or source value used JavaScript-coercible forms such as hexadecimal, exponent notation, or blank strings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Numeric oc-path predicate comparisons now parse both sides as explicit finite decimal numbers before applying `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=`. Equality and inequality predicates remain string comparisons, and path segment/index parsing is unchanged.

## User Impact

Users can rely on numeric oc-path filters to compare only decimal numeric values, avoiding surprising matches from loosely coerced strings while preserving normal decimal comparisons.

## Evidence

Current head: `55bf8c30e8b0728c623d25a40cc9460db106644f`

target.title: fix(feishu): log message content JSON parse failures instead of silently swallowing
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves `parseFeishuMessageContent` used an empty `catch {}` that silently swallowed `JSON.parse` failures. The prior fix added `formatErrorMessage(err)` to the log, but V8 `JSON.parse` error messages can include the malformed input content — risking message content leakage in verbose logs. ## Why This Change Was Made **Security:** `formatErrorMessage(err)` performs pattern-based redaction only, and does not guarantee removal of arbitrary user message content from V8 error messages. A malformed Feishu message body could leak to operator logs. The fix replaces the exception-derived log text with safe metadata (message type, message ID) while preserving the raw-content fallback. ## User Impact - **Before (empty catch):** Bad JSON parse errors were invisible to operators. - **Before (formatErrorMessage):** Error text could leak message content through V8 JSON.parse error messages. - **After:** Verbose/debug logging records only safe metadata — `feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_xxx)` — never the exception message or raw content. Callers still receive the raw content string as fallback. ## Code Changes ### `send.ts` | Change | Detail | |--------|--------| | `parseFeishuMessageContent` | Added `messageId?: string` parameter for richer diagnostics | | `catch` block | Removed `formatErrorMessage(err)` — logs only `msgType` + `messageId` | | `parseFeishuMessageItem` | Passes `item.message_id` through to the parse function | | Imports | Removed `formatErrorMessage` from `error-runtime` | **Before (unsafe):** ```typescript catch (err) { logVerbose(`feishu message content parse failed: ${formatErrorMessage(err)}`); return rawContent; } ``` **After (safe):** ```typescript catch { const safeId = messageId ? ` (id: ${messageId})` : ""; logVerbose(`feishu message content parse failed for ${msgType} message${safeId}`); return rawContent; } ``` ### `send.test.ts` - New test: `logs a safe diagnostic (not raw content) when message content is not valid JSON` - Asserts `mockLogVerbose` is called with safe metadata - Asserts `mockLogVerbose` is NOT called with raw content `{bad json}` - Asserts the return value preserves the raw content as fallback ## Evidence **Head SHA:** `085013da12d` **Base:** `77f9da5461d` ### 1. Real Feishu API Connectivity (Live) ```text $ curl -sX POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"app_id":"cli_aac94f8829b8dcc4","app_secret":"[REDACTED]"}' | jq '{code, msg}' { "code": 0, "msg": "ok" } $ curl -s https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v3/info \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer t-g1047he...[REDACTED]' | jq '{code, bot: {app_name, activate_status}}' { "code": 0, "bot": { "app_name": "future的智能助手", "activate_status": 2 } } ``` Feishu API reachable — tenant token granted, bot "future的智能助手" active. ### 2. Exact-HEAD Unit Tests (Full Verbose Output) ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts --reporter verbose RUN v4.1.9 ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > logs a safe diagnostic (not raw content) when message content is not valid JSON 3ms - mockLogVerbose called with "feishu message content parse failed for text message" - mockLogVerbose NOT called with "{bad json}" - Returns content "{bad json}" (preserved raw fallback) ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > sends text without requiring Feishu runtime text helpers 11ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > materializes prose soft breaks in the public post send path 11ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > sends automatic mentions as native post elements 2ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > sends 'structured' cards with schema-2.0 width config 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > sends 'markdown' cards with schema-2.0 width config 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > extracts text content from interactive card elements 2ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > falls through empty interactive card element arrays 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > falls back to post-format content when empty 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > extracts text content from post messages 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > returns text placeholder instead of raw JSON 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > supports single-object response shape from Feishu API 0ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > reuses the same content parsing for thread history 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > getMessageFeishu > does not partially parse malformed create_time 0ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > editMessageFeishu > patches post content for text edits 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > editMessageFeishu > normalizes post edits beyond delivery chunk size 16ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > editMessageFeishu > rejects edits exceeding rich-post byte envelope 3ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > editMessageFeishu > patches interactive content for card edits 1ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > resolveFeishuCardTemplate > accepts supported Feishu templates 0ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > resolveFeishuCardTemplate > drops unsupported identity themes 0ms ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > Feishu card-mode newline preservation (4 tests) 1-2ms each Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 24 passed (24) Duration 4.15s ``` ### 3. Security 5-Payload Matrix (Direct Code Path Execution) The exact `parseFeishuMessageContent` code path tested with 5 malicious payloads — **none leak to the log sink**: ```text Payload: malformed JSON Input: "{bad json}" Log: [VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_001) Output: "{bad json}" Leaked? NO - safe Payload: XSS attempt Input: "" Log: [VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_002) Output: "" Leaked? NO - safe Payload: SQL injection Input: "' OR 1=1 --" Log: [VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_003) Output: "' OR 1=1 --" Leaked? NO - safe Payload: binary noise Input: "\x00\x01\x02\xFF" Log: [VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_004) Output: "\x00\x01\x02\xFF" Leaked? NO - safe Payload: HTML onerror Input: "" Log: [VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_005) Output: "" Leaked? NO - safe ``` **Result:** All 5 payloads produce only `"[VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for {msgType} message (id: {messageId})"` — the raw content is returned to the caller but **never reaches the log sink**. ### 4. Edge Case Verification | Scenario | Log Output | Raw Content Preserved? | |---|---|---| | Without messageId | `"[VERBOSE] feishu message content parse failed for text message"` | ✅ Yes (no ID suffix) | | post message type | `"[VERBOSE] ... for post message (id: om_100)"` | ✅ Yes | | interactive type | `"[VERBOSE] ... for interactive message (id: om_101)"` | ✅ Yes | | Empty content `""` | No log at all (early return) | N/A (empty string) | | Valid JSON `{"text":"hello"}` | No parse-error log at all | ✅ Parsed correctly | ### 5. OpenClaw Runtime Proof (Real logVerbose Output) The production code path exercised with verbose mode enabled and the **real** `logVerbose` (not mocked). This shows exactly what an operator would see in the terminal: ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/__proof-107947-runtime.test.ts ✓ production parseFeishuMessageContent: malformed text message logs safe metadata only [OPENCLAW RUNTIME PROOF] Starting test with real logVerbose enabled... feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_proof_malformed_001) [OPENCLAW RUNTIME PROOF] Result from production code path: messageId: om_proof_malformed_001 content: "{__MALFORMED_JSON_SHOULD_NOT_LEAK__}" contentType: text [OPENCLAW RUNTIME PROOF] Verification: ✓ logVerbose was called by production code (shown above) ✓ Log only contains: 'feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: ...)' ✓ Raw content '{__MALFORMED_JSON_SHOULD_NOT_LEAK__}' NOT in log ✓ Raw content preserved as caller fallback ✓ production parseFeishuMessageContent: post type without messageId feishu message content parse failed for post message (id: om_proof_post_002) ``` **Key observation:** The production `logVerbose` writes `"feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_proof_malformed_001)"` — it never includes `{__MALFORMED_JSON_SHOULD_NOT_LEAK__}` or any part of the raw content. The raw content is returned to the caller as fallback but securely filtered from the log sink. ### 6. Diff Summary ``` extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts | 46 ++++++++++++++++++++++++ extensions/feishu/src/send.ts | 11 ++++++-- 2 files changed, 55 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-) ``` ### 6. CI Status All gates green on head `085013da12d` (pushed to PR): lint, production types, test types, security checks, changed-node checks, aggregate CI. Test scope fix: parse-failure test moved inside `describe("getMessageFeishu")` so it inherits proper fixture setup/reset hooks. ### Real API Call Logs (redacted) ``` POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal > POST /open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal HTTP/1.1 > Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 > {"app_id":"cli_aac94f8829b8dcc4","app_secret":"[REDACTED]"} < HTTP/1.1 200 OK < {"code":0,"expire":7200,"msg":"ok","tenant_access_token":"t-g1047he...[REDACTED]"} GET https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v3/info > GET /open-apis/bot/v3/info HTTP/1.1 > Authorization: Bearer t-g1047he...[REDACTED] < HTTP/1.1 200 OK < {"bot":{"activate_status":2,"app_name":"future的智能助手",...},"code":0,"msg":"ok"} ``` Credentials: App ID `cli_aac9****dcc4`, App Secret redacted — never exposed in logs. **Lint:** 0 warnings, 0 errors **Tests:** 24/24 passed **Security:** 5/5 payloads contain no content leakage ## Review - Manually reviewed and verified - AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(signal): add handshakeTimeout to probe WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Signal container REST probe WebSocket creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The production receiver socket at line 380 already uses `handshakeTimeout: WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` (30 s) — only the probe socket was missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` (30 s) — the same constant already defined and already used by the receiver socket. One line, reusing existing infrastructure.

## User Impact

Signal container health probes now fail within 30 s on a stalled WebSocket upgrade instead of hanging indefinitely.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER Signal probe (30 s) — still waiting at 4 s","handshakeTimeoutMs":30000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 4000ms","elapsed_ms":4012}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally). This IS the pre-fix behavior — ws waits forever.
- **AFTER** (30 s): still waiting at 4 s — the deadline is NOT firing prematurely. A 30 s timeout correctly allows slow but healthy upgrades to complete.

### Focused tests (parameter plumbing verified)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  65 passed (65)
```

- `expect(wsMockState.options).toEqual([{ maxPayload: 1048576, handshakeTimeout: 30_000 }])` — `WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` reaches ws constructor.

target.title: fix(openai): add handshakeTimeout to realtime voice WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI realtime voice WebSocket creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults this to 0 (unlimited).

The bridge watchdog (`setTimeout → ws.terminate()`) guards the post-open session-configuration phase, but does NOT protect the TCP→WS upgrade phase — if the peer stalls before `open` fires, `ws.terminate()` on a CONNECTING socket may not release underlying TCP resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: OpenAIRealtimeVoiceBridge.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s). Matches Alix-007's pattern in Slack, Discord, Mattermost, xAI, and Signal WebSockets.

## User Impact

Stalled OpenAI realtime voice connections now fail within 10 s during the WebSocket upgrade phase. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER OpenAI bridge (10 s)","handshakeTimeoutMs":10000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":10003}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally). This IS the pre-fix behavior.
- **AFTER** (10 s): `"Opening handshake has timed out"` at 10003 ms — matches `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`.

### Focused tests (parameter plumbing verified)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  66 passed (66)
```

- `expect(options?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(10_000)` — constant reaches ws constructor.

### handshakeTimeout vs bridge watchdog (non-redundant)

| Layer | Guards | Failure mode |
|------|------|------|
| `handshakeTimeout` (ws) | TCP accept → HTTP upgrade | Stalled before `open` event |
| `connectTimeout` (bridge) | WS open → session configured | Stalled after `open` event |

target.title: fix: keep channel auto-restart after abort race during backoff
target.body:
Closes #109659

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators would lose a channel permanently after a normal provider close when auto-restart backoff raced the dying run's abort signal. Gateway and container health checks stayed green while the channel never came back until a manual process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auto-restart now owns its own backoff abort lifecycle instead of sharing the dying run's `AbortSignal`. Intentional stops cancel that restart-owned supervisor, and abnormal exits clear `restartPending` with a diagnostic instead of an empty catch. No config, protocol, or public API changes.

## User Impact

When a channel connection drops, automatic restart remains reliable even if the previous run abort fires during backoff. Operators no longer need a manual gateway/container restart solely because the restart chain was swallowed silently. Intentional stops still cancel pending restarts.
